items.title: [Windows] Pet overlay causes the ChatGPT desktop window to flicker and jump while dragging

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 26.1007.21434, build 13901 ### What subscription do you have? plus ### What platform is your computer? Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0 x64 ### What issue are you seeing? Description The ChatGPT desktop app’s main window flickers and appears to jump between positions while being dragged after it approaches, overlaps, or interacts with the floating pet. The issue reproduces with both built-in and custom pets. Other applications’ windows do not exhibit this behavior. Hiding the pet eliminates the issue. Environment - OS: Windows, x64 - App version: 26.1007.21434 - Build: 13901 - Installed package: OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64 - Update check on October 12, 2026: up_to_date ### What steps can reproduce the bug? Steps to reproduce 1. Open the ChatGPT desktop app. 2. Show a floating pet, either built-in or custom. 3. Move the main window near or across the pet, or interact with the pet. 4. Drag the main window around. 5. Hide the pet and repeat the dragging operation for comparison. ### What is the expected behavior? Expected behavior The main window moves smoothly, regardless of whether the pet is visible or nearby. Actual behavior With the pet visible, dragging the main window causes flickering and apparent jumps to previous positions. Hiding the pet stops the problem. ### Additional information

Troubleshooting performed

Test | Result -- | -- Switch from a custom pet to a built-in pet | Still reproduces Hide the pet | Issue disappears Drag other applications’ windows | No equivalent issue observed Fully restart ChatGPT with --disable-gpu | Still reproduces Check for an app update | No update available

The GPU test was verified through the running processes:

  • Main process included --disable-gpu.
  • Renderer processes included --disable-gpu-compositing.
  • GPU service included --use-angle=d3d11-warp-webgl.

Disabling hardware acceleration therefore did not resolve the issue.

Recording

Attachment: Desktop 2026.10.12 - 12.28.05.01.mp4

The recording is approximately 17.45 seconds long, at 2560 × 1440 resolution. Around 8.10–8.16 seconds, the main window visibly alternates between positions. The recording alone cannot establish whether this is an actual native window-position change or presentation of stale frames.

Possible cause — not confirmed

Read-only inspection of the installed application bundle found that the pet overlay’s applyPointerInteractivityPolicy() includes a path calling:

setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })

The symptoms closely resemble Electron issue #35030, which reports that mouse forwarding on a secondary window can cause another window in the same application to flicker while being dragged.

This is a potential lead, not a confirmed root cause. The installed application also contains an input-shape path, and the active runtime branch during reproduction has not been traced.

Suggested investigation

Check whether the pet overlay’s mouse forwarding interferes with the main window’s native move/resize loop on Windows. Consider testing whether temporarily suspending forwarding during movement or resizing, then restoring the appropriate interaction state afterward, resolves the issue without breaking pet hover or click-through behavior.

Impact and current workaround

The issue makes it difficult to keep the pet visible while repositioning the main window. The only verified workaround so far is to hide the pet.

items.title: Windows sandbox setup adds AppContainer ACE to the whole user profile and crashes other Electron apps on launch

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

items.body:
Related to #15777, which was filed on March 25 and is still open. This is a separate issue because it needs its own fix and is hitting more than the browsers reported there.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300

### What issue are you seeing?

The Windows sandbox setup puts an explicit, inheritable full-control ACE for its "Exebox Sandbox" AppContainer SID (`S-1-15-2-1907908163-…`) on `C:\Users\<name>` itself. Every folder under the profile inherits it, including `AppData\Local` and everything installed there. It does not add the matching `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` (`S-1-15-2-1`) entry.

Electron's startup check (`install_dir_access.cc`) fails when a directory has an AppContainer entry but no `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` entry. I hit this with the Gemini desktop app: the launcher stayed running, the app itself crashed six times, and the crash dump read:

> Sandboxed processes cannot read C:\Users\<name>\AppData\Local\Google\Gemini\app-1.14.0: its ACL has an entry for an AppContainer package SID but none for ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES.

There was no window and no error dialog. I only found the cause by reading crash dumps.

How I traced it to the Codex sandbox (circumstantial, I did not see the change happen):

- `icacls C:\Users\<name>` shows the AppContainer ACE as explicit (not inherited) on the profile root. `AppData`, `AppData\Local` and `AppData\Local\Google\Gemini` only inherit it.
- The SID is registered under `HKCU\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppContainer\Mappings` with the moniker `exebox-sandbox-…` and the display name "Exebox Sandbox".
- The same ACLs carry a `CodexSandboxUsers` group, `codex-windows-sandbox-service` is running, and `~\.codex\.sandbox` exists.
- #15777 reports the same root cause and attributes it to the sandbox setup.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install Codex on Windows and complete the sandbox setup.
2. Run `icacls "%USERPROFILE%"` and look for the AppContainer ACE with no `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` entry.
3. Install any Electron or Chromium app under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (Gemini desktop in my case) and launch it.

### What is the expected behavior?

Installing the sandbox should not change the permissions of the whole user profile or stop other apps from launching.

- Scope the ACE to the directories the sandbox actually uses (`.codex\.sandbox` and so on) rather than the profile root.
- If the root must be touched, grant `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` read alongside it.
- Warn the user, and provide a cleanup path, when setup changes ACLs outside Codex's own directories.

### Additional information

Workaround (grants read to all packages on the profile; this fixed Gemini without removing any Codex entries):

`icacls "%USERPROFILE%" /grant *S-1-15-2-1:(OI)(CI)(RX)`

items.title: Support user-managed persistent context regions with dynamic replacement

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop app on Windows

### What feature would you like to see?

## Use case

I already have an external framework that identifies the user's current intent, assembles the applicable rules, and loads them into the conversation. When the intent has not changed, it should reuse the same rule snapshot. When the intent changes, it should replace that snapshot with the newly assembled rules. The source of these rules does not need to be a fixed file or directory.

Currently, repeatedly appending rules to the conversation can accumulate stale or conflicting copies. AGENTS.md, configuration, and hooks are useful, but they do not provide the complete live, replaceable persistent-context mechanism needed for this workflow.

## Requested behavior

Please support user-managed persistent context regions with dynamic replacement:

1. Allow an authorized user or plugin to set, read, replace, and clear a named context region.
2. Support both stable regions and dynamic regions, with explicit scope and instruction precedence.
3. Include the current version in every model request, including tool-follow-up requests, without appending duplicate copies to the conversation on each call.
4. Apply updates atomically at a defined request boundary and return the active version, so a caller can determine which snapshot a request uses.
5. Define where these regions appear in the assembled context, such as a designated prefix and an optional tail, while respecting the instruction hierarchy.
6. Preserve the current regions across compaction and session resume. Superseded revisions must not become active again. Keep revision history or audit records separate from the active context.

## Scope and constraints

Intent recognition and rule assembly would remain the responsibility of the external framework. This request is for a reliable context carrier and lifecycle, not a new intent-classification system.

The regions would still consume normal context/token capacity. This is not a request for zero-cost context or guaranteed perfect model compliance. Existing authorization, security boundaries, and instruction hierarchy must remain intact. Prompt caching and incremental request handling should remain correct when a region changes.

## Acceptance example

- Load rule snapshot A into a dynamic region.
- Make multiple model requests, including tool follow-ups. Each uses A without accumulating duplicate copies.
- When the intent changes, replace A with snapshot B at the defined request boundary.
- Subsequent requests, including after compaction or session resume, use B as the active snapshot and do not restore A.
- Historical conversation messages that mention A do not need to be erased; they simply must not reactivate A as the current managed region.

### Additional information

Related but different requests:

- #14814 discusses pre-turn injection of dynamic metadata. This request is about managed regions with replace-in-place semantics, a current version, and persistence across requests.
- #46337 discusses replacing conversation history at compaction time. This request does not ask to replace the conversation transcript; it asks to preserve the current managed regions through compaction and resume.

items.title: [Desktop][macOS] Scheduled task produces an empty response; processed follow-up remains in queued message UI

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Environment
- macOS desktop app, ChatGPT Work mode
- Model shown: GPT-6.1 Sol, light reasoning
- Observed on October 12, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai)
- Exact app/macOS versions and subscription: not collected

## Problem
The user reports this has happened repeatedly recently. Three screenshots show inconsistent conversation and queued-message state around a scheduled task and a permission request.

## Observed sequence
1. A scheduled task posts a monitoring prompt into an existing conversation.
2. The assistant shows a running-command state and a permission dialog asking whether to allow a read-only production status check. A follow-up user message is displayed above the composer with a waiting indicator and delete icon.
3. A later screenshot shows the turn as completed after 19 seconds, with response action icons but no response text. The follow-up remains in the waiting row. The screenshots do not establish which permission option was selected.
4. In a subsequent screenshot, another user prompt has a normal conversation bubble and receives a response. A further instruction remains in the waiting row even though the assistant has already begun responding specifically to that instruction. The app shows Thinking and an active Stop button at this point.

## Expected behavior
- A turn should produce a visible response or a clear cancellation/error state.
- Once a queued/steered instruction has been consumed, its UI state should update consistently instead of continuing to appear pending.
- Scheduled-task execution, permission handling, turn completion, and queued-message display should remain synchronized.

## Evidence and limits
This report is based on three user-provided screenshots, not an independently reproduced trace. The strongest evidence is that an instruction remains in the pending row while the assistant is already responding to it. The earlier conclusion that the message was simply never sent would be inaccurate.

No backend logs or feedback ID were collected. Screenshots are not uploaded here because they contain unrelated private business conversation details; the relevant visible states are described above. Root cause is unknown, and no claim is made that the permission dialog alone caused the issue.

## Possibly related
#19951 describes delayed/queued/steered prompt inconsistencies and UI/backend state divergence. Similar symptoms do not establish an identical cause.

ChatGPT Pro — personal account

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After switching from Codex to ChatGPT Work in the Windows desktop app, most settings disappear and I cannot switch back to Codex.

Observed symptoms:

Settings only shows General, Appearance, and Personalization.

Usage information is unavailable.

The account menu only shows my email address, Settings, Help, and Logout.

I cannot return to Codex through the mode selector.

In-app feedback submission is also rejected with a message indicating that I do not have permission.

Restarting the app and signing out and back in with the same ChatGPT account do not resolve the issue.

I am using my usual personal account. The same account displays an active Pro subscription on the ChatGPT website.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Sign in to the Windows desktop app using a personal ChatGPT Pro account.

Start in Codex mode.

Open the mode selector and select ChatGPT Work.

Open Settings and check the available sections and usage information.

Attempt to switch back to Codex using the mode selector.

After the transition, most settings and usage information are unavailable, and switching back to Codex is not possible.

### What is the expected behavior?

Switching between Codex and ChatGPT Work should preserve a valid account session. I should be able to return to Codex through the mode selector, access the relevant settings and usage information, and submit feedback without changing my sign-in method.

### Additional information

Temporary recovery method:

Sign out of the desktop app.

Sign in using an API key. The missing settings reappear at this point.

Switch to Codex mode.

Sign out again.

Sign back in using the original ChatGPT account.

This sequence restores access to Codex, but it is only a workaround.

Diagnostic observations:

App logs from October 12, 2026, around 13:22–13:23 KST (04:22–04:23 UTC), contain these messages and fields:

Workspace routing is unavailable
Statsig: error while bootstrapping post-login client
authenticatedAccountPresent=false
authMethod=chatgpt
failureType=account_info_request_failed
remote control enrollment is waiting for a ChatGPT account id

Requests to these endpoints also fail:

/wham/usage
/settings/user

Before discovering this issue, I had been unable to sign in to the desktop app for approximately one week. Sign-in eventually worked after uninstalling and reinstalling the app. I do not know whether the earlier login issue is related.

I am reporting this through GitHub because in-app feedback submission is also blocked by a permission error.

items.title: Windows desktop Remote: new projectless chat fails with “Unable to resolve projectless chat folder”

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary
Creating a new projectless chat from a Windows laptop on a connected Windows desktop host fails before the first prompt is submitted:

```text
Error submitting message
Unable to resolve projectless chat folder
```
Existing remote chats continue to work. Creating a new chat from the host side in an existing project also works, providing a verified workaround.

## Environment
- Date observed: 2026-10-12
- Both client and host: Windows
- Windows app package version on both machines: `26.1007.2314.0`
- Host internal app version: `26.1007.21434`
- Host bundled session service version reported during diagnosis: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`
- Connection: Settings → Connections → Control other devices (Remote Control), **not SSH**
- Host shows connected with a green indicator.
- Host update check reported no eligible update on its configured channel.

## Reproduction
1. Pair/connect the Windows laptop to a Windows desktop through Control other devices.
2. Switch the app surface to Codex.
3. Start a new chat; select Remote and the connected desktop host.
4. Leave Choose project unset.
5. Enter a prompt and submit.

## Expected
A working directory is resolved/created on the remote host and the new chat starts.

## Actual
Submission fails with the error above. Restarting the laptop app does not resolve it. Opening and continuing an existing remote chat succeeds.

Client log excerpt (identifiers and unrelated data omitted):
```text
Error creating local task errorMessage="Unable to resolve projectless chat folder"
[Composer] submit failed cwd=~ errorMessage="Unable to resolve projectless chat folder" followUp=none mode=local
```
The log's `mode=local` label is included verbatim; the UI was set to Remote.

## Read-only investigation
Inspection of the installed app's projectless-directory resolution code found the error is thrown after canonical path resolution returns no value or a non-absolute path. A read-only reproduction on the Windows host using the generated PowerShell path-resolution command failed with an unexpected-token syntax error involving the directory argument (anonymized example: `C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Codex`). This points to argument quoting/construction in the remote Windows path-resolution command. This is our diagnosis, not an upstream-confirmed root cause.

Both the default directory and the host's custom task directory exist. Inspection also indicated that the remote projectless branch uses the remote user's default directory rather than the host desktop's customized projectless directory, so changing that setting is not a demonstrated workaround.

## Verified workaround
From a working existing chat on the desktop host, use the app's create_thread tool targeting an existing local project and its local environment. One new chat was successfully created, opened from the laptop, and confirmed its working directory and machine name on the desktop host. No project was re-added and no project files were modified.

## Related UX observation (may be separate)
The laptop's Choose project menu displays its own saved projects and New remote project, but does not display the host desktop's existing saved projects even after selecting the remote host. The host-side list_projects tool can enumerate those existing projects. Please clarify whether reuse/discovery of host-saved projects is supported; we are not asserting this observation has the same root cause as the submission failure.

No installation files, configuration, databases, or migration flags were modified during diagnosis. Full logs and private conversation links are intentionally omitted.

items.title: [Windows][Codex Desktop] One conversation and later fork fail with request-processing errors; earlier-history fork recovers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

App-server technical logs identify the client as **Codex Desktop 26.1007.21434**. This version has not been independently confirmed in the About dialog.

The affected conversation and both inspected forks record **codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2**, with **paginated** history.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT sign-in. The subscription plan is Pro 5x

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, OS build 26200.

### What issue are you seeing?

One existing conversation develops repeated request-processing errors and eventually fails. Other unrelated conversations continue to work normally. A fork retaining the more recent history reproduces the same failure, while forking at an earlier history point lets the work continue and complete two subsequent turns.

The error is:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: An error occurred while processing your request.
You can retry your request, or contact us through our help center at help.openai.com
if the error persists. Please include the request ID 308ea133-d04a-4021-9f5e-7e788b7f1bea in your message.
```

Some retries recover temporarily and the assistant continues producing messages/tool calls. The affected original turn and the later fork still terminate after their final retry sequences. This is not a claim that every request fails immediately.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed with the existing affected history on **2026-10-12**; I do not have a standalone deterministic reproducer:

1. Continue an existing coding conversation using **gpt-6.1-sol**, **xhigh**.
2. Complete a diagnostic turn about timeouts/incomplete streaming responses in a separate external evaluation workload.
3. Ask for a retry-policy change, approximately: “Automatically retry requests when no response headers arrive or a long streaming response is interrupted.” The Codex turn repeatedly retries and ultimately fails with the error above.
4. Fork while retaining that completed diagnostic turn and request the same kind of retry-policy change. The fork also ultimately fails.
5. Fork from an earlier history point, omitting the diagnostic turn, and request the same kind of work. This branch completes the work and a subsequent follow-up turn.

This comparison changes the history cutoff and is not a controlled comparison with byte-identical prompts, simultaneous requests, or identical live backend state. It narrows a suspicious interval; it does not prove a corrupted item.

### What is the expected behavior?

An otherwise valid conversation should remain usable after continuing or forking. If a retained history item or resume state cannot be processed, Codex should surface an actionable error and provide a supported recovery path that preserves useful context, rather than only exhausting generic retries.

### Additional information

**Read-only local evidence** confirms the branch comparison:

| Branch alias | Observed outcome | Sampling retry log entries | Relevant successful-response input accounting |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A_ORIGINAL | Final turn fails at 02:32:55 UTC | 15 | Last reported input: 224,771 tokens |
| B_LATER_FORK | Fork turn fails at 02:42:20 UTC | 12 | Last reported input: 222,029 tokens |
| C_EARLIER_FORK | Two subsequent turns complete, at 03:27:08 and 03:47:30 UTC | 1 transient retry, recovered | Maximum observed successful input: 295,284 tokens |

All three branches use the same model/effort. The reported context window during the incident is **475,000 tokens**. These are successful-response usage snapshots, not measured sizes of failed requests. The successful branch handling a larger input weakens a simple input-token cutoff explanation, but does not rule out payload-specific limits or backend behavior.

The failing route is **HTTP Responses**, to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`. The final retry attempts receive **HTTP 200**, followed by the stream/request-processing error. The final error classification is `codex_error_info: other`; HTTP 200 does not imply a completed model response.

The selected provider is a custom label `aigw` named `OpenAI`, with `requires_openai_auth = true` and `supports_websockets = false`. No `base_url` override is present in its current configuration. The incident logs independently identify the same label and first-party ChatGPT HTTP route. I have not performed controlled alternate-network or proxy experiments.

The two fork cutoffs are **60 stored records apart** (exclusive cutoffs 34038 and 34098). Mapping those cutoffs to the original session identifies one completed diagnostic turn, plus its surrounding settings records, between **02:08:46 and 02:17:14 UTC** (local timezone UTC+08:00):

- 3 tool calls and 3 corresponding tool returns, all text.
- 10 persisted reasoning items.
- No typed image item and no compaction record in this interval.
- One text output contains normal truncation markers; its largest text block is 40,102 characters.
- JSON parsing, call/return pairing, text-character checks and reasoning Base64 syntax checks find no obvious structural corruption. Base64 validity does not validate encrypted reasoning content, and file-local checks do not validate all inherited history.

The separate evaluation workload's own transport errors are **not** being treated as the cause of Codex's errors. This report concerns the first-party Codex response failures.

#### Request IDs for backend correlation

Complete request IDs are now included with my authorization so OpenAI maintainers can correlate the failing requests with backend logs. Representative terminal failures:

| Branch | Terminal failure time (UTC) | Request ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A_ORIGINAL | 2026-10-12T02:32:55.633Z | `308ea133-d04a-4021-9f5e-7e788b7f1bea` |
| B_LATER_FORK | 2026-10-12T02:42:20.618Z | `404d3c63-50ea-4d06-a8df-a9138a5a4844` |

The diagnostic attachments include all **29 distinct request IDs** present in the selected retry and terminal-error records, alongside the existing stable request aliases. The recovered transient retry in C_EARLIER_FORK did not contain a request ID in the inspected error message. Original conversation/thread and turn IDs remain omitted publicly.

#### Supporting attachments

[Sanitized diagnostic files](https://gist.github.com/Kevin589981/7a2d725f0d1bd2844a853f5cdff91c67):

- `diagnostics-summary.json`: environment, fork cutoffs, branch outcomes and structural statistics.
- `redacted-events.jsonl`: selected lifecycle, retry, HTTP-status, compaction and usage events with stable aliases and complete request IDs.
- `evidence-notes.txt`: collection method and interpretation limits.

Complete request IDs are included in this issue and its attachments for backend correlation. Original conversation/thread and turn IDs remain omitted publicly and are retained offline for private follow-up if needed. No credentials, authorization/cookie headers, account identifiers, original prompts/answers, encrypted reasoning, project paths, tool commands or private service addresses are attached. Source session records and application settings were not modified during collection.

#### Related reports

- #27681: one resumed thread fails with the same error while other chats work; HTTPS fallback also fails.
- #19433: failures persist in particular resumed sessions while others stay stable.
- #51889: a later-history fork fails while an empty control chat initially works; different macOS/WebSocket symptoms.
- #18960: a commenter recovered a history-dependent fork failure by cleaning large image payloads. That specific image mechanism is not established here, since the identified interval has no image item.

The additional evidence here is an **earlier-versus-later fork boundary on the same conversation ancestry**, under the same model/effort, with the working branch subsequently handling more input tokens. Could maintainers investigate history/resume handling around this boundary, correlate the attached request IDs with backend logs, and advise on a supported recovery or a narrower diagnostic export?

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0 ### What subscription do you have? GPT Plus ### What platform is your computer? Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 ### What issue are you seeing?

After an apparent Codex Desktop update around October 10, 2026, the Windows application began failing to complete ChatGPT authentication.

The login interface displays the following error:

Sign-in could not be completed

Token exchange failed: error sending request for url
(https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token)

Error code: token_exchange_failed

Before this update, I had been using Codex with a TUN-based global proxy configuration without authentication problems. Occasional network instability previously caused interrupted responses, but did not cause login failures or repeated sign-outs.

Since the update, I have observed:

  • Codex Desktop cannot reliably complete the ChatGPT OAuth login process.

  • Repeated workspace routing discovery timeouts in the application logs.

  • Multiple HTTP 432 responses with Workspace routing is unavailable.

  • The ChatGPT desktop application unexpectedly requires authentication again after Windows restarts. This occurred after two separate restarts and was not previously observed.

  • ChatGPT remains accessible through a web browser, although response performance is sometimes slow.

The installed package version is OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.

Diagnostic logs collected over the most recent three days contain:

Log pattern | Occurrences -- | -- workspace routing discovery timed out | 20 Workspace routing is unavailable | 22 status=432 | 23 account/read | 88 CRYPT_E_REVOCATION_OFFLINE | 0 certificate verify failed | 0

These are keyword occurrence counts, not necessarily distinct failures. In particular, the account/read count includes all matching log entries, not exclusively errors.

The token_exchange_failed message is displayed in the login UI, but that exact string was not found in the inspected application log files.

The onset closely coincides with the application update. However, I cannot yet determine whether the underlying cause is an application regression, changed proxy handling, authentication/workspace routing behavior, or a combination of these factors.

### What steps can reproduce the bug? The bug could be reproduced by simply restart the computer and then open Codex (ChatGPT) again. Detailed steps are shown below: 1. Run Codex Desktop for Windows, version `26.1007.2314.0`. 2. Use a local proxy application with TUN mode and global routing enabled, which previously worked consistently. 3. Launch Codex Desktop and attempt to sign in using an existing ChatGPT account. 4. Complete the browser-based authentication flow and return to Codex. 5. Observe the `token_exchange_failed` error during OAuth token exchange. 6. Inspect the local Codex Desktop logs and observe repeated workspace routing discovery failures, timeouts, and HTTP 432 responses. 7. Switch from TUN mode to the Windows system proxy while keeping global proxy routing enabled, and retry authentication. The login issue persists. Additional observation: After restarting Windows on two separate occasions, the ChatGPT desktop application also required a fresh login, despite previously retaining authentication across system restarts. This issue is reproducible in my current environment, but I have not confirmed whether it also occurs without a proxy or on earlier application versions. ### What is the expected behavior? Codex Desktop should successfully exchange the OAuth authorization code for an access token, complete ChatGPT authentication, and initialize account and workspace routing. Previously authenticated desktop sessions should normally remain available across application and Windows restarts, provided the session is still valid. Temporary network interruptions should not unnecessarily invalidate locally persisted authentication state. If workspace routing or token exchange fails because of a transient network condition, the application should provide a recoverable error and allow a retry without requiring repeated full authentication. ### Additional information **Update and runtime information** - Codex Desktop package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0` - Approximate onset: October 10, 2026, following an apparent application update. - Local runtime executable: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\2e5e00daee91c61d\codex.exe` - Runtime executable last modified: October 10, 2026, at 17:18:52 (local time). This timestamp is consistent with the suspected update period but does not independently establish the package installation time. **Network configuration** - Local HTTP proxy: `127.0.0.1:X` - Previously working configuration: TUN mode + global proxy routing. - Also tested: Windows system proxy + global routing. - Proxy nodes have shown intermittent connectivity problems and elevated latency. **OAuth endpoint connectivity test** A request containing deliberately invalid OAuth parameters was sent directly to the relevant endpoint through the local HTTP proxy: ```powershell curl.exe -sS -D - -o NUL ` --max-time 60 ` --proxy "http://127.0.0.1:X" ` -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" ` --data "grant_type=test" ` -w "HTTP=%{http_code} TLS-ready=%{time_appconnect}s Total=%{time_total}s Exit=%{exitcode}`n" ` "https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token" ``` The test completed successfully at the HTTP transport level: ```text HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request HTTP=400 TLS-ready=14.356540s Total=15.949031s Exit=0 openai-processing-ms: 10 ``` The HTTP 400 response is expected because the OAuth parameters were deliberately invalid. This confirms that the endpoint is reachable through the proxy and can process requests, although TLS establishment is unusually slow. Earlier diagnostic attempts also produced connection timeouts and intermittent Schannel TLS errors, indicating potentially unstable network conditions. Additional diagnostic finding: I executed `login status` using the exact `codex.exe` bundled with my Codex Desktop installation (`26.1007.2314.0`). The result was: ``` Logged in using ChatGPT ``` However, the Desktop application still fails after browser authorization with: ``` Sign-in failed: workspace routing discovery timed out ``` My logs also contain repeated `account/read` failures, workspace routing discovery timeouts, and HTTP 432 (`Workspace routing is unavailable`). This indicates that local ChatGPT authentication state is present and recognized by the bundled CLI, while the Desktop application is unable to complete account/workspace initialization. My explicit-proxy test of the OAuth token endpoint returned HTTP 400 as expected, with a TLS establishment time of 14.36 seconds. The possibility of a workspace-routing timeout interacting with high network latency may be worth investigating. **Related issues** - #52996 — Same Windows desktop version with HTTP 432 workspace routing failures and account lookup problems. - #53055 — Same desktop version with repeated workspace routing discovery failures and reconnect behavior. The application update may have changed authentication or networking behavior in a way that makes previously tolerated network instability more disruptive. However, causality has not been established. I would appreciate guidance on whether this is a known regression in `26.1007.2314.0`, and whether a fix or supported workaround is available that does not require deleting local authentication data or changing a previously working system-wide proxy configuration.

items.title: Offer a quota-free background mode with bounded compute and durable task continuation

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: rate-limits
labels.description: Issues related to rate limits, quotas, and token usage reporting

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App

### What feature would you like to see?

An opt-in **background execution mode without hard per-user 5-hour or weekly exhaustion**, using bounded account-level compute, fair scheduling, durable checkpoints and automatic continuation instead.

The goal is not infinite simultaneous GPU capacity. It is to let a paid user leave an autonomous workflow running overnight without having to wake up and manually restart it at a quota boundary.

### Problem

I use a $200 Pro subscription for long-running coding tasks. I have started work before bed and found that usage exhaustion stopped it overnight. More nominal weekly usage does not necessarily solve this: a restrictive short window can still interrupt the workflow while the weekly balance is sufficient.

I recognise that [the current documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-using-codex-with-your-chatgpt-plan) already says an active turn may continue after a usage limit is reached, subject to fair-use limits. This request goes beyond that grace behaviour: it concerns durable continuation of an entire workflow across turns, temporary resource shortages and allowance boundaries.

### Proposed modes

**Preferred: quota-free background execution.** Bound aggregate compute and concurrent expensive jobs per account, including child agents. Share a capacity-capped pool fairly, with unused capacity available to active users. Keep the selected model and reasoning settings unchanged. Queue or pace work at safe boundaries rather than terminating the workflow or silently downgrading its model.

**Transitional: priority allowance, then background service.** Keep a normal-speed allowance, but make exhaustion a change of scheduling priority rather than a hard stop. Be explicit that this still has a usage-dependent priority threshold; it is not the fully quota-free design.

**Minimum improvement: durable suspend and auto-resume.** If quota changes are not feasible, checkpoint the workflow, display its state and reset time, and resume automatically once permitted. This improves unattended operation but does not remove limits.

For all modes, expose `running`, `capacity-queued`, `quota-suspended`, and `needs-approval` as distinct states. Do not promise overnight completion when the queue cannot support it. Automatic continuation must be opt-in, cancellable and bounded by a user-selected deadline; it must not grant new permissions, silently enable paid overages, replay non-idempotent tool actions, or override outstanding approval requests. Paused tasks should not require indefinitely pinned GPU memory.

### A reproducible synthetic evaluation

I do not have OpenAI's utilisation, hardware-cost, model-cost or workload telemetry. The attached Python study therefore uses **explicitly hypothetical normalised compute units**, not estimated GPU counts, tokens, subscription entitlements or dollars.

The main grid contains **960 runs: 8 policies × 6 offered-load levels × 20 seeds**, plus 60 short-window sensitivity runs. Each run has 100 synthetic accounts, 28 days, a 7-day warm-up and 5-minute scheduling steps. Short jobs have 4-hour deadlines; overnight jobs have 8-hour deadlines. The exact same workload is replayed under each policy for a given seed/load.

Importantly, **every simulated policy already resumes automatically when eligible**. The quota baseline is not deliberately penalised by forcing the user to sleep through a reset. No restart waste, caching gains, cheaper models or quality improvements are assumed. "Finished" means the specified compute service was delivered, not that generated code passed a real evaluation.

The reference pool has a service-rate ceiling of 12 NCU (12 NCU-hours of service per hour). The illustrative weekly allowance is 12 compute-unit-hours per account; its doubled version is 24. The illustrative rolling 5-hour allowance is 2 compute-unit-hours. **These are study parameters, not Codex limits.**

At 75% offered load, the seed-mean results were:

| Policy | Overnight jobs finished within 8h | Executed compute relative to weekly-only |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weekly allowance only; concurrency 4 | 24.0% | 1.00× |
| 2× weekly allowance; no 5-hour cap | 60.7% | 1.40× |
| 2× weekly allowance + rolling 5-hour cap | 20.2% | 1.39× |
| No volume quotas; concurrency 2 | 88.4% | 1.59× |
| Priority allowance, then spare-capacity service | 87.8% | 1.59× |
| No volume quotas; lower pooled service ceiling | 0.0% | 1.26× |

The first five rows use the same physical service ceiling. The final row deliberately lowers it from 12 to 7.14 NCU: `100 accounts × 12 weekly units / 168 hours`. This matches the reference allowance's **long-run aggregate service envelope**, not its actual observed spending or a dollar budget. Since offered work is 9 NCU-hours per hour in this scenario, that lower ceiling is insufficient and its queue grows.

## Additional information

The reproduction bundle includes `simulate.py`, `METHODOLOGY.md`, `RESULTS.md`, all per-seed JSON results and a time-resolution check. It runs locally on CPU, makes no API/network calls and needs no credentials.

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python simulate.py --self-test
python simulate.py --out results
```

For a shorter run: `python simulate.py --seeds 3 --loads 0.35 0.75 1.25 --no-sensitivity --out quick_results`.

[continuous_compute_proposal.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33318912/continuous_compute_proposal.zip)

### Additional information

_No response_

items.title: [macOS] ChatGPT 26.1007.30912 crashes ~60-100s after launch, SIGTRAP at identical Codex Framework offset 0x475d754 (7/7 reproductions)

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT 26.1007.30912 (build 20156) Codex Framework 155.0.8059.40 (Auto-updated on 2026-10-11 09:11 local time; the app worked fine before that update.)

### What subscription do you have?

Pro 20

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm，macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Mac17,5, Apple Silicon, 8 GB RAM

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop app launches, stays alive for 60-100 seconds without any interaction, and then dies with EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP). This is fully deterministic: 7 crashes on 2026-10-12, all with the *identical* base-relative faulting offset inside Codex Framework: 0x475d754.

Crash facts (identical in all 7 reports):

- Exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP), exception code 0x1
- Triggered thread: 0, CrBrowserMain, dispatch queue com.apple.main-thread
- Termination reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 5, Trace/BPT trap: 5
- Faulting instruction: brk #0
- Faulting offset: 0x475d754 (Codex Framework, base-relative; framework is stripped)
- Threads at crash: 66-70, composition identical every time:
    ThreadPoolForegroundWorker x16, NetworkConfigWatcher x14,
    (unnamed) x4-6, libuv-worker x4, V8Worker x3, ThreadPoolBackgroundWorker x3
- Engine log stop: ~2 minutes of normal startup activity, then the log just stops

Crash table (all identical offset):

  1. 09:24:53  70 threads   0x475d754
  2. 09:25:56  67 threads   0x475d754
  3. 09:27:22  69 threads   0x475d754
  4. 09:32:49  68 threads   0x475d754
  5. 09:35:05  68 threads   0x475d754
  6. 11:04:19  66 threads   0x475d754
  7. 11:22:33  70 threads   0x475d754

Top frames of the crashing thread (nearest exported symbols; the framework is stripped):

  0  Codex Framework  ares_llist_replace_destructor + 24448     <- faulting instruction (brk #0)
  1  Codex Framework  ares_llist_replace_destructor + 24340
  2  Codex Framework  v8::Signature::New(...) + 15777116
  ...
  19 Codex Framework  node::InternalCallbackScope::Close() + 400
  20 Codex Framework  node::InternalMakeCallback(...) + 464
  22 Codex Framework  node::Environment::CheckImmediate(uv_check_s*) + 256
  23 Codex Framework  uv__run_check + 128
  24 Codex Framework  uv_run + 620
  ...
  30 CoreFoundation    __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_SOURCE0_PERFORM_FUNCTION__

The crash happens inside a Node/V8 callback driven from the main-thread run loop, in the uv_run "check" phase, immediately after an immediate callback runs.

Note on 0x475d754: this matches, bit for bit, the V8 OOM callback address independently disassembled in #52631. This looks like a V8 fatal-error BRK rather than a data abort.

IMPORTANT: this does NOT look like the SkyComputerUseService spawn storm reported in #38455 / #40153 / #38744:

- Only 66-70 threads at crash (vs ~316 threads / 187 computer-use threads in #38455)
- No SkyComputerUseService helper processes were present on this machine before or after any crash (verified with pgrep; the only leftovers were browser_crashpad_handler orphans and a bare-modifier-monitor)
- No unbounded thread growth in the 60-100s window

So this may be a different root cause reaching the same V8 fatal-error path.

In the engine's own log (~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite, 21k+ rows) there is no heap / OOM / allocation-failure warning at all. The last engine log line is during normal startup (config/batchWrite, plugin/list, skills/list, remote plugin catalog fetch, MCP server startup) and then logging simply stops - consistent with the fatal error happening in the Chromium/V8 main process rather than the Rust engine.

7 .ips reports are attached, renamed to .txt because GitHub does not accept .ips.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Fully quit ChatGPT and terminate any leftover helper processes (browser_crashpad_handler, bare-modifier-monitor, extension-host).

2. Launch /Applications/ChatGPT.app normally (double-click from Finder/Dock).

3. Do absolutely nothing. Do not start a task, do not invoke Computer Use, do not send a message.

4. Open Activity Monitor and watch the process; after roughly 60-100 seconds the app exits with SIGTRAP and macOS shows the "ChatGPT quit unexpectedly" dialog.

5. Relaunch: it crashes again with the same offset. Reproduced 7/7 times.

Things that do NOT change the outcome (each tried, app relaunched, crashed again at 0x475d754):

- Disabling plugins: computer-use@openai-bundled, unified-computer-use@openai-bundled, browser@openai-bundled, chrome@openai-bundled (all set enabled = false)
- Disabling MCP servers: ssh-mcp-server, chrome-mcp-server, node_repl (all set enabled = false)
- Commenting out the notify hook that points at SkyComputerUseClient
- Verifying my edits survived the app's own config/batchWrite (they did)
- Rebooting the machine, quitting and relaunching the app many times
- Cleaning ~/.cache/codex-runtimes of failed runtime-install leftovers (1.2 GB reclaimed)

Environment checks that came back clean:

- codesign --verify --deep --strict passes; spctl reports accepted / Notarized Developer ID; TeamID 2DC432GLL2; CDHash 73332b93baf1f0bc5ed95ca079cfa6aeceecb677
- Every path referenced from config.toml exists and versions match, including Contents/Resources/cua_node/bin/node_repl, Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/.../codex, and ~/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-bundled/browser/26.1007.30912/scripts/browser-service.mjs (cache version matches the app version exactly)
- config.toml is valid TOML
- CODEX_HOME (~/.codex) is a regular directory, NOT a symlink, so this is not the symlink-triggered leak of #39732
- 57 GB free disk space, no memory-pressure kill involved

A network note that is probably unrelated but visible in the logs: on this machine plaintext DNS for chatgpt.com is hijacked by the ISP/campus network, and Node's fetch ignores the system proxy, so Node-side calls fail with "TypeError: fetch failed" (also seen as: MCP server stderr (npx): Fatal error: TypeError: fetch failed). Requests routed through the local proxy do reach chatgpt.com fine (HTTP 426 in ~1.2s on the remote-control upgrade endpoint). The pre-crash retry pattern does not correlate with the crash instant.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should stay running while idle. If an internal helper cannot complete its bootstrap handshake, the app should apply a retry limit / exponential backoff / circuit breaker instead of dying with a fatal V8 error ~90 seconds after launch.

An idle desktop app must not terminate itself deterministically within two minutes of launch.

I would also expect the engine log to contain some diagnostic output before a fatal V8 error - currently the log just stops with no warning.

### Additional information

Timeline:

- Before 2026-10-11: the app worked normally on this machine.
- 2026-10-11 09:11: the app auto-updated (Sparkle PersistentDownloads timestamp matches; the binary's signature timestamp is 2026-10-10 13:32).
- 2026-10-12 09:24 onwards: deterministic crash loop begins.

The Codex CLI on the SAME machine is unaffected: codex-cli 0.151.0 works normally. Only the desktop app crashes.

There is no older build available to roll back to on this machine, and the app reports auto-update enabled with no user-visible way to pin or downgrade a version.

Hardware context that may matter: this machine has only 8 GB of RAM, so an app-side memory blow-up would hit the V8 heap limit quickly.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: sandbox

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

X5

### What platform is your computer?

win 10 pro

### What issue are you seeing?

Hi Codex team,
I’m using Windows 10 Pro and have updated the Codex desktop app to the latest version available to me. I continue to encounter several issues that affect everyday use, and some became noticeable after the update.
1. Sandbox and Tool Execution Failures
Codex frequently encounters sandbox or execution-environment problems when performing local tasks. Errors I have encountered include:
- helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors
- Failed to create unified exec process
- spawn EPERM
- Access is denied / Windows error 5
In some cases, commands fail before they actually start. In others, a routine local operation cannot run inside the sandbox and requires an additional approval to retry outside it.
I understand that some operations legitimately require elevated permission. The problem is that it is difficult to distinguish an expected permission restriction from a failure in the sandbox or execution environment. These interruptions make routine development work unreliable and lead to repeated approvals, retries, and troubleshooting.
Please improve the reliability of the Windows sandbox and make errors clearly distinguish between permission restrictions, process-launch failures, and sandbox initialization failures.
2. Missing Code Change Summaries
After Codex modifies code, the UI no longer consistently displays the summary showing:
- Which files were modified.
- The number of lines added and removed, such as +20 / -8.
- The entry point for reviewing the changes.
The code changes may exist locally, but the expected summary is missing from the response or interface. This makes it harder to review the work and verify its scope without manually inspecting Git diffs.
3. All Projects Disappeared After the Update
After updating Codex, all projects disappeared from the Projects section of the sidebar. However, conversations under Pinned and Recent were still visible and accessible.
Local investigation found that the project definitions and conversation records still existed, while the sidebar’s local project configuration was empty. Restoring the configuration while Codex was running did not persist; recovery had to be performed while the application was fully closed.
An application update should preserve project organization and conversation associations. If migration fails, there should be a clear recovery option rather than leaving the Projects section empty.
4. The Selected Interface Language Is Not Respected When Restarting Offline
I changed the interface language from English to another supported language. However, if Codex is restarted without internet access, the interface falls back to English instead of retaining the selected language.
The language preference is still saved locally, and the translation resources are included in the installation. Local inspection suggests that translation loading also depends on a feature configuration that defaults to disabled when unavailable.
Please ensure that an explicitly selected interface language remains effective during offline startup and does not depend on a successful network request.
5. Conversation Titles Are Incorrect Until the Conversation Is Opened
Some sidebar entries initially display an old title, a file path, or text from a historical message instead of the correct conversation title.
Clicking the conversation causes the title to change to the correct one. This suggests an inconsistency between the initial sidebar data and the data loaded when opening a conversation.
Please make the sidebar display the saved conversation title correctly from startup, without requiring users to open conversations individually.
Impact and Request
These issues interrupt development, make reviewing code changes more difficult, and force users to spend time repairing the tool instead of doing their work. Disappearing project organization also creates understandable concern about whether work or conversation history has been lost.
The Windows version of Codex urgently needs reliability improvements. For users, these problems can disrupt daily work and reduce confidence in the product. For OpenAI, persistent instability may lead users to switch to other tools.
Please prioritize investigating these issues on Windows 10 Pro, particularly update migrations, sandbox execution, code-change summaries, offline language persistence, and sidebar consistency.
We can accept a slower release cycle, but we cannot accept every new version introducing a different set of problems. These are not just recurring issues; new and unrelated failures keep appearing with each update. Please prioritize stability and regression testing over release frequency.
Thank you.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment
- OS: Windows 10 Pro
- App: Codex desktop, updated to the latest version available to my installation
- Installed version observed during investigation: 26.1007.2314.0
- Existing local projects, pinned conversations, and conversation history
1. Sandbox / Tool Execution Failures
1. Open an existing local project in Codex on Windows.
2. Ask Codex to inspect local files or perform a development task that requires shell commands.
3. Allow Codex to execute the commands using the sandbox.
4. In affected runs, execution fails during environment initialization or process creation, sometimes before the command starts.
Actual: Errors may include helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors, Failed to create unified exec process, spawn EPERM, or Windows “Access is denied.” Some operations require an additional approval and a retry outside the sandbox.
Expected: Commands permitted by the configured sandbox policy should run reliably. Legitimate permission denials should be clearly distinguished from sandbox initialization or process-launch failures.
Reproducibility: Intermittent. I do not currently have a single command that reliably triggers every failure. Not every access-denied error necessarily represents the same underlying issue.
2. Missing Code Change Summary
1. Open a local Git project.
2. Ask Codex to modify one or more source files.
3. Wait for Codex to finish.
4. Confirm that the files were changed using the editor or git diff.
5. Check the completed response and its associated change-review UI.
Actual: In affected runs, the modified-file summary and added/removed line counts are not displayed even though the files were changed.
Expected: The completed task should display the changed files, the + / - line counts, and an accessible way to review the diff.
Reproducibility: Intermittent; observed during normal coding tasks.
3. Projects Disappear After Updating
1. Start with a Codex installation containing multiple local projects, pinned conversations, and recent conversations.
2. Update the application to the affected release.
3. Reopen Codex and inspect the sidebar.
Actual: The Projects section is empty, while pinned and recent conversations remain accessible. Local investigation found that project records still existed, but the sidebar project configuration was empty.
Expected: Updating the application should preserve existing projects and their conversation associations.
Reproducibility: Observed after updating my existing installation. A fresh installation may not reproduce this; testing should include migration from an installation with existing project data.
4. Interface Language Falls Back to English Offline
1. While online, select a supported interface language other than English.
2. Confirm that the interface displays the selected language.
3. Fully exit Codex, including its system-tray process.
4. Disconnect the computer from the internet.
5. Launch Codex again and inspect the sidebar, menus, and settings.
Actual: The interface displays English instead of the saved language.
Expected: The saved interface language should remain effective when starting offline.
Reproducibility: Repeatedly observed on my machine. Please test a full application restart, not just closing and reopening the window.
5. Conversation Titles Correct Themselves Only After Opening
1. Start Codex with existing conversations that have saved or previously renamed titles.
2. Inspect the sidebar before opening those conversations.
3. Find an entry displaying an old title, a path, or historical message text.
4. Click that conversation and observe the sidebar title again.
Actual: The title changes to the correct saved title only after the conversation is opened.
Expected: The sidebar should display the correct saved title immediately, without requiring each conversation to be opened.
Reproducibility: Affects some existing conversations, not necessarily every conversation or every startup.

items.title: [dot cloud browser] New-tab navigation fails approval after repeated consent without actionable recovery

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

On 2026-10-12, approximately 02:54–03:07 UTC, opening WhatsApp Web in dot's cloud browser failed before the website opened, despite repeated explicit user authorization and a retry after renewed approval.

The intended task was to open WhatsApp Web and begin its phone-number linking flow. The failure happened before any login step.

Observed error text included:
- "JavaScript execution did not receive approval"
- On a later attempt: "browser security check was unavailable" and "permission request was dismissed before a decision"
- The later result also stated that no explicit denial was made

These are the captured error excerpts, not a claim to reproduce the complete diagnostic output.

Browser inventory showed only a blank new tab. WhatsApp Web never opened. The failed call returned no actionable approval card or browser-handoff link.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed incident sequence; reproducibility in a fresh session is not established:

1. From the macOS app, ask dot to open WhatsApp Web using dot's cloud browser.
2. Explicitly authorize that action.
3. Attempt the normal browser action:

`cua.createBrowserTab('cdp', 'https://web.whatsapp.com/')`

4. Receive a missing-approval error before navigation completes.
5. Give renewed explicit approval and retry the same action.
6. Receive a browser-security-check-unavailable / permission-request-dismissed result, with no explicit denial recorded and no usable approval or handoff path.
7. Check browser inventory: only a blank new tab is present.

### What is the expected behavior?

The applicable permission flow should complete and open the authorized page. If an additional decision is required, the user should receive an actionable prompt. If the approval service or browser-security check is unavailable, the error should identify that state accurately and provide a supported recovery path.

Repeatedly asking for consent must not leave the user stuck in the same failed action without anything they can approve or fix.

### Additional information

Environment:
- Conversation surface: macOS app
- Execution surface: dot's cloud browser
- Exact client, browser and backend versions were not captured

Impact and complaint:
The user repeatedly approved a basic browser action but could not make progress. This wasted time, blocked the requested task, and undermined confidence in the assistant's reliability. Please investigate the permission-request lifecycle and the missing actionable recovery flow.

The underlying cause is unknown. This report does not establish a WhatsApp login problem, a website-generated denial, a service-wide outage, or who/what dismissed the permission request.

Possibly related, but not established duplicates:
- #50734: a cloud-browser file upload stalls and then reports a dismissed permission request
- #51475: cloud-browser page reads fail approval after handback

This incident adds a failure during initial new-tab navigation, before any website content or login flow was reached.

This report contains only the minimal technical sequence and user-visible failure. Personal contact details, login codes, credentials, private account content, raw conversations, and internal identifiers are omitted.

## Summary

- Windows 11
- Codex Desktop build 26.1007.2314.0
- Local host
- Reproduced after reboot and after restarting the app

Existing local projects and their chats should remain visible and grouped in the sidebar across an app update and reboot.

This appears related to issues #35088 and #39121, where local projects and/or recent tasks remain in backend/local state but disappear from the Windows desktop sidebar.

items.body:
The remote marketplace serves `superpowers@openai-curated-remote` **6.4.2**, while obra/superpowers released **v7.0.0** on 2026-10-10 (https://github.com/obra/superpowers/releases/tag/v7.0.0). The public `openai/plugins` repository is further behind at 6.3.0 (`plugins/superpowers/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` on `main`).

`codex plugin list` on codex-cli 0.162.1 (Linux, WSL2):

```
superpowers@openai-curated-remote  installed, enabled  6.4.2  plugins~Plugin_60aea7460bd4819199fd97a9553a5e12
```

Claude Code, OpenCode and Antigravity on the same machine run 7.0.0 from the upstream marketplace, so Codex is the one harness a release behind, and only the curated catalog can move it.

Related:
- #29517 - the same request, for 6.0.3
- #45260 - the curated copy ships Superpowers' helper scripts without the executable bit (upstream 100755, OpenAI's copy 0644); a re-sync is a chance to fix both

**Ask:** re-sync the curated Superpowers plugin to v7.0.0, or document the cadence at which the remote catalog follows upstream releases so users know what to expect.

Several consecutive turns in that chat failed, including very short follow-up messages. The chat history remains readable, but subsequent turns do not complete reliably. Other Codex chats on the same app and network continue to work.

5. Send a message in another Codex chat on the same machine and network; that chat works.

The failures were observed repeatedly on 2026-10-12 around 10:27–10:49 China Standard Time (UTC+8). No network-switch test has been performed.

### What is the expected behavior?

The affected chat should complete a new turn normally. If its persisted state is damaged or a stream fails, the app should offer a recoverable retry or resume path without losing the chat history.

### Additional information

The thread identifier and request IDs were supplied privately to OpenAI through the Help Center support chat. They, along with conversation content, local logs, file paths, and business information, are omitted from this public issue. Please provide a secure channel if maintainers need narrower diagnostics.

Related reports show similar error text, but the key distinction here is that repeated failures are isolated to one existing chat while other chats continue to work.

items.title: [Windows] Chrome plugin fails: browser-client not trusted and Native Host registration missing

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.2314.0

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

On Windows, the Codex App Chrome plugin is installed and enabled, but browser initialization consistently fails with:

```
privileged native pipe bridge is not available; browser-client is not trusted
```

The failure occurs before Chrome tabs can be retrieved.

The bundled Chrome Native Messaging Host executable exists, but its manifest and registry registration are missing.

Reinstalling the Chrome plugin from the Codex plugin UI does not resolve the issue.

## Environment

- OS: Windows x64
- Codex App Windows package: 26.1007.2314.0
- Internal app version reported in config: 26.1007.21434
- Chrome plugin version: 26.616.32156
- Browser plugin version: 26.616.32156
- Subscription: ChatGPT Plus

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Codex Windows App.
2. Enable the bundled Chrome plugin.
3. Start a new Codex session.
4. Ask Codex to list open Chrome tabs using the official Chrome plugin.
5. The Node REPL loads `browser-client.mjs` and attempts to initialize it.
6. Initialization fails before any Chrome tab information is retrieved.

## Actual Behavior

The following error is consistently reproduced:

```
privileged native pipe bridge is not available; browser-client is not trusted
```

The official Native Host diagnostic reports:

```json
{
  "registryManifestPath": null,
  "exists": false,
  "correct": false,
  "problem": "Windows native host registry key does not exist; Native host manifest does not exist"
}
```

Both the expected HKCU and HKLM Native Messaging Host registry keys are absent.

The expected manifest file is also missing:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\extension\com.openai.codexextension.json`

## Additional Diagnostics

- `node_repl.exe` exists and multiple Node REPL processes are running.
- `extension-host.exe` exists in the bundled Chrome plugin directory.
- The Chrome plugin's `latest` junction correctly points to version 26.616.32156.
- Both bundled `browser-client.mjs` files have the same SHA-256 hash.
- `NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES` is configured with the browser service.
- The Chrome plugin remains installed and enabled.
- A fresh Codex session reproduces the failure.
- Chrome installation detection returned `installed_browsers: []`, but this result alone does not establish that Chrome is missing.
- The Chrome running state could not be verified because the diagnostic `tasklist` command failed.

## Troubleshooting Already Attempted

- Reinstalled the Chrome plugin through the Codex plugin UI.
- Verified bundled plugin files and junction targets.
- Verified Node REPL executable and running processes.
- Ran the official Native Host manifest checker.
- Tested browser initialization in a new Codex session.

The issue persists.

No manual registry changes, configuration modifications, or unsupported Native Host installation attempts were performed.

## Expected Behavior

The Codex Chrome plugin installation should correctly register its Native Messaging Host.

The official browser client should be trusted by the Codex runtime and receive access to the privileged Native Pipe Bridge, allowing Chrome tab enumeration and browser interaction.

## Request

Please investigate:

1. Why the bundled Chrome plugin installation does not create the Native Host manifest and HKCU registry registration.
2. Why the official `browser-client.mjs` is not trusted by the Node REPL runtime.
3. Whether the Native Host installation failure and privileged Native Pipe Bridge failure share a common root cause.
4. Whether a supported repair procedure or application update can resolve the issue.

Related reports: #28950 and #21781.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch the Codex Windows App (package version 26.1007.2314.0).
2. Verify that the bundled Chrome plugin is installed, enabled, and displayed as managed.
3. Open a new Codex session.
4. Ask Codex to list the currently open Chrome tabs using the Chrome plugin.
5. Codex attempts to initialize the official `browser-client.mjs` through Node REPL.
6. Initialization fails with the following error:

```
privileged native pipe bridge is not available; browser-client is not trusted
```

7. The Chrome tab list cannot be retrieved.

**Reproducibility:** Consistently reproducible, including in new Codex sessions.

**Troubleshooting already performed:**
- Reinstalled the Chrome plugin from the Codex plugin UI.
- Verified that the bundled plugin files exist.
- Verified that `node_repl.exe` is running.
- Confirmed the same initialization error after reinstalling the plugin.

The issue persists.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Codex Windows App should successfully initialize the official Chrome browser client through Node REPL.

The bundled Chrome plugin should automatically install and register its Native Messaging Host, including the required manifest file and Windows registry entry.

The browser client should be recognized as trusted and have access to the privileged Native Pipe Bridge.

Codex should then be able to retrieve open Chrome tabs and perform supported browser interactions without initialization errors.

### Additional information

## Environment

- Windows x64
- Codex App package: 26.1007.2314.0
- Internal app version reported in config: 26.1007.21434
- Chrome plugin: 26.616.32156
- Browser plugin: 26.616.32156
- ChatGPT Plus

## Native Host diagnostics

The official `check-native-host-manifest.js --json` reports:

```
"registryManifestPath": null
"exists": false
"correct": false
```

Missing registry key:

`HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts\com.openai.codexextension`

The equivalent HKLM key is also absent.

Missing manifest file:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\extension\com.openai.codexextension.json`

## Plugin and runtime checks

- Bundled `extension-host.exe` exists.
- Bundled `installManifest.mjs` exists.
- Chrome plugin `latest` junction correctly targets version 26.616.32156.
- Both bundled `browser-client.mjs` files have identical SHA-256 hashes.
- Multiple `node_repl.exe` processes are running.
- `NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES` contains a browser-service entry.
- `NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_BROWSER_CLIENT_SHA256S` was not found in the inspected configuration.
- Chrome installation detection returned `installed_browsers: []`, but Chrome installation status remains unconfirmed by that diagnostic.

The bundled troubleshooting documentation explicitly advises against manually installing or repairing the Native Host.

No unsupported manual repair or registry modification was performed.

## Investigation requested

Please investigate whether the missing Native Host registration and the privileged Native Pipe Bridge trust failure originate from the same Windows Codex App initialization problem.

Related reports: #28950 and #21781.

items.title: apply_patch drops trailing spaces from filenames

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

This is a minor edge case, but Linux supports filenames ending in a space. Codex's `apply_patch` silently removes that space and writes to a different file. Gemini CLI and OpenCode handle the same filename correctly with their write tools.

Observed on Linux at Codex commit `ca466061d64f0b44f416135c7fd06aa7af850bbc`. The same parsing code remains on `main` at `a9b0815167c27ab13719dd12d13b63e02b70d221`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a file whose name ends in one space:

```sh
printf 'old\n' > 'notes.txt '
```

Call `apply_patch` with this patch. The Add File header must have one space immediately after `notes.txt`:

```text
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: notes.txt 
+hello
*** End Patch
```

Expected: write `hello\n` to `notes.txt `.

Actual: Codex reports success adding `notes.txt`, creates that file with `hello\n`, and leaves `notes.txt ` unchanged. This simplified reproduction follows the same code path as the recorded test, which used `zu.log `.

### What is the expected behavior?

See above

### Additional information

_No response_

items.title: [Windows][Auto-review] Reviewer claims read-only/no escalation for workspace-write/on-request session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434 — About dialog: ChatGPT, Powered by Codex & OWL; released October 9, 2026 (user-confirmed)

### What subscription do you have?

API key authentication; not signed in with a ChatGPT account. ChatGPT subscription not used for this session.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.6456

### What issue are you seeing?

On October 12, 2026, auto-review repeatedly denied an explicitly authorized, narrowly scoped update to the CodeGraph/GitNexus rules block in `%USERPROFILE%/.codex/AGENTS.md`. The file is outside the workspace writable roots, so the agent requested `require_escalated` through the normal approval mechanism.

The denial acknowledged the limited scope and user authorization, but claimed that the current environment was read-only and escalation was prohibited. The displayed Chinese rationale included:

> 当前执行环境为只读，且策略禁止申请提权，因此不能批准此写操作。

English translation: “The current execution environment is read-only, and its policy prohibits requesting escalation; therefore this write cannot be approved.”

Renewed user authorization did not resolve the denial. A subsequent read-only check of this task's permission records was also denied as a supposed attempt to work around the earlier rejection.

**Evidence from the main session:**
1. Five recent main-agent `turn_context` records all showed `sandbox_mode=workspace-write` and `approval_policy=on-request`.
2. Four records used `approvals_reviewer=auto_review`; the later manual-approval record used `user`. The workspace roots and network restrictions were unchanged.
3. The task state also recorded `approval_mode=on-request` and workspace write permissions.
4. Local configuration had no explicit override for `approval_policy`, `approvals_reviewer`, or `sandbox_mode`, and no custom auto-review policy.
5. After switching the desktop approval control from “Approve for me” to manual approval and approving the escalated operation, the requested update succeeded with exit code 0.
6. Readback confirmed the reviewed block was applied exactly and all other rule blocks were preserved. The permission-record check also succeeded in read-only mode after switching.

The user then restored automatic approval; we did not repeat the completed write. The incorrect explanation blocked a small configuration edit and related diagnosis until the user switched approval modes.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start a Windows desktop session using `workspace-write` / `on-request` and “Approve for me”.
2. Explicitly authorize a small, reviewed change to a user configuration file outside the workspace writable roots.
3. Request the change using `require_escalated`.
4. Compare any “read-only / escalation prohibited” denial with the main-agent permission records.
5. Switch to manual approval and approve the corresponding operation; compare execution and effective sandbox settings.

The proposed change only clarified index maintenance triggers and reminders. It did not alter sandbox or approval settings, grant privileges, or disable a security control.

This describes the observed sequence; it is not a claim that every session reproduces the issue. No full session or raw internal log is attached.

### What is the expected behavior?

Auto-review should evaluate the effective permissions and authorization of the requesting main session. An operation may be declined for an applicable policy reason, but the explanation should not assert read-only / prohibited escalation when the recorded main session is workspace-write / on-request and supports approval requests.

If another immutable managed policy applies, identify that constraint rather than attributing unsupported permissions to the main session.

### Additional information

The confirmed finding is a mismatch between the rejection rationale and the main-session permission records. Reviewer context or permission attribution may be involved, but the responsible component is unknown and an undisclosed managed policy cannot be fully excluded. We do not claim a confirmed Windows ACL fault or a specific version regression.

Authentication is via API key with a configured custom model provider; whether provider/model differences affect this behavior has not been isolated. No API key, provider endpoint, credentials, production data, real usernames, company paths, or complete task transcript are included.

We checked related reports #52019 and #47234. This report focuses on the explicit read-only/escalation-prohibited rationale conflicting with main-session records, plus the successful manual-approval comparison. #52019's original records instead showed never/danger-full-access/user; #47234 focuses on local policy edits and policy reload.

This report was prepared by Codex and submitted with the user's explicit authorization.
