items.body:
## Problem

The macOS desktop app records two recurring control/startup failures:

1. `model/list` expires after approximately 30 seconds **in the app-server request queue**.
2. Local Work executor startup repeatedly fails while waiting for `plugin/installed`.

Please investigate both the queued-request lifecycle and the plugin-discovery dependency during executor startup. The available evidence does not establish a common root cause.

## Environment

- Installed ChatGPT desktop app / Codex compatibility bundle ID: `com.openai.codex`.
- App version: `26.1007.30912`; build: `20156`, read from the installed application's Info.plist.
- Incident logs also report build `20156` and commit `a993bdbe5bb9503cb84de1e67d5635cf186a959f`.
- macOS: `26.6.2`, reported by Python's `platform.mac_ver()` during this inspection.
- Observation date: October 11, 2026. All timestamps below are UTC.
- Bundled app-server version and subscription tier were not collected.

## Verified diagnostic evidence

These are selected, field-preserving excerpts from existing desktop logs. Identifiers, local paths and unrelated fields are omitted.

### A. Model discovery expires while queued

```text
2026-10-11T14:56:26.896Z warning [AppServerConnection]
  app_server_client_request_queue_rejected
  method=model/list source=models priority=background
  inFlightRequestCount=8
  queuedBackgroundRequestCount=5
  queuedCriticalRequestCount=1
  queuedInteractiveRequestCount=21
  queuedPriorityRequestCount=5
  queueWaitMs=30000 reason=queue-expired

2026-10-11T14:56:26.899Z error [electron-message-handler]
  Request failed method=model/list durationMs=30002
  error={"code":-32001,"message":"App server request expired while queued"}
```

The rejection record explicitly reports a 30-second queue wait. This should be distinguished from model inference latency or a confirmed remote model-service timeout.

### B. Plugin response timeout prevents Local Work executor startup

A separate launch sequence records:

```text
2026-10-11T14:59:11.584Z info [tpp-local-executor]
  Starting Local Work executor attempt=1

2026-10-11T14:59:41.335Z warning [electron-message-handler]
  mcp_request_timeout method=plugin/installed source=plugins
  priority=background queueWaitMs=0 timeoutMs=30000

2026-10-11T14:59:41.586Z warning [tpp-local-executor]
  Local Work executor startup failed attempt=1
  errorMessage="Timed out waiting for MCP response to plugin/installed"

2026-10-11T14:59:46.080Z warning [AppServerConnection]
  app_server_client_request_queue_rejected
  method=plugin/installed source=plugins priority=background
  inFlightRequestCount=8 queueWaitMs=29999 reason=queue-expired

2026-10-11T15:00:12.602Z warning [tpp-local-executor]
  Local Work executor startup failed attempt=2
  errorMessage="Timed out waiting for MCP response to plugin/installed"
```

The same launch log records the same executor failure for attempts 3–6 at 15:00:43.607, 15:01:14.612, 15:01:45.616 and 15:02:16.621 UTC. These are logged startup attempts, not user/model turns.

The immediate demonstrated impact is failed Local Work executor startup. Why plugin discovery does not complete, and whether the model-list queue expiry shares that cause, remain unverified.

## Reproduction status

This is a report based on an existing user profile and retained application logs. A deterministic clean-profile reproduction and the initiating user action have not been established. No stress test, configuration change, history deletion or installed-app modification was performed for this report.

## Expected behavior / requested investigation

- Model discovery should complete or return an actionable, bounded failure while keeping essential controls responsive.
- Local Work startup should expose a clear plugin-discovery failure and a supported recovery path.
- Diagnostics should distinguish queue expiry from a dispatched request waiting for a response.
- Please investigate in-flight request age/completion and the specific plugin-discovery operation blocking executor startup; the log's count of eight is an observation, not a claim that the scheduler's implementation has been proven.
- Recovery should preserve existing conversations.

## Separate authorization error

The same installation also records `thread/read` / `source=thread_hydration` returning `-32003: thread access denied`, including responses with `queueWaitMs=0`. That is a separate authorization-error class, tracked in #53178. Its co-occurrence does not establish that it causes these queue/startup failures.

Increasing memory or deleting conversation history is not an established remedy for that access denial and cannot be presented as a guaranteed fix. Please preserve authorization boundaries while investigating the read path.

## Related reports checked

- #50812: Windows desktop reports involving eight occupied host RPC slots and read timeouts.
- #51905: Windows/WSL Local Work startup waiting for `plugin/installed`.
- #53178: macOS repeated access-denied background hydration.

These are related signatures, not confirmed shared root causes; please consolidate if appropriate.

items.title: node_repl leaves an empty .tmpXXXXXX in TMPDIR on every signal shutdown (thousands accumulate on macOS)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21159 (bundled `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`, `cua_node/bin/node_repl`)

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant. This is local process behaviour.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2, arm64

### What issue are you seeing?

`node_repl` leaves one empty `.tmpXXXXXX` directory in `$TMPDIR` every time it starts and is stopped by a signal. The Codex app starts it for every thread and subagent. On one Mac this added up to **7,882 empty `.tmp*` directories in the user temp dir** (`getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR`), about 686 a day. They accumulated in one flat directory alongside other tools' temp files. A directory that large slows every create and readdir in it, and the churn showed up as a large share of `fseventsd` load during a machine slowdown.

Each directory is created when `node_repl` starts (the kernel assets temp dir, I assume). It is removed only on a graceful shutdown (stdin EOF), and is left behind on SIGTERM or SIGKILL.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Standalone, with `node_repl` started using the `[mcp_servers.node_repl]` command and env the app writes into `~/.codex/config.toml`, and a private `TMPDIR`:

1. Start `node_repl` with `TMPDIR=/tmp/repro/tmp/`, send MCP `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`.
2. `/tmp/repro/tmp/` now contains one `.tmpXXXXXX`.
3. Stop the process:
   - close stdin (EOF): exits 0, and the directory is removed ✅
   - `SIGTERM`: the empty `.tmpXXXXXX` remains ❌
   - `SIGKILL`: the empty `.tmpXXXXXX` remains ❌ (expected; nothing can run)

Through the app server: an isolated `CODEX_HOME` whose only MCP server is that `node_repl` entry, with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty dir. Run `codex app-server`, send `initialize` / `initialized` / `thread/start`, wait for `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated` → `ready`, then close stdin. One empty `.tmpXXXXXX` remains. With a minimal third-party stdio MCP server in place of `node_repl`, nothing remains, so the app server's own path is clean. The leak is in how `node_repl` handles a signal shutdown, and that is how it gets stopped.

### What is the expected behavior?

`node_repl` should remove its temp dir on SIGTERM as well as on EOF: handle the signal and drop the `TempDir` before exiting. Alternatively, the app server could close the MCP server's stdin and wait briefly before signalling. Either way, a dir left by a SIGKILLed run could be reaped on the next start. Placing it under a per-app subdirectory (e.g. `$TMPDIR/codex/`) would also keep it out of the shared flat temp dir.

### Additional information

The leftovers are always empty, so this costs inodes and directory size rather than bytes. Two related observations from the same machine, in case they're useful: the Codex desktop app (Electron) also left 1,548 `.com.openai.codex.*` files (74 MB, mostly copies of bundled JS, fonts and SVGs) in the same directory over three days.

By Merlin ([rbeckner.com](https://rbeckner.com)) and his AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5, thinking on: low).

items.title: install.sh: verify_archive_digest clobbers global archive_path, overwriting checksum manifest with package archive

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

latest (main / 0.142.5 - 0.159.0)

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### Which model were you using?

N/A (Installer)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Terminal / zsh / Ghostty

### Codex doctor report

```json
"not applicable (installer script bug before binary invocation)"
```

### What issue are you seeing?

In `scripts/install/install.sh`, `verify_archive_digest()` assigns its first argument to `archive_path`:

```sh
verify_archive_digest() {
  archive_path="$1"
  expected_digest="$2"
  actual_digest="$(file_sha256 "$archive_path")"
```

Because POSIX `/bin/sh` does not scope function variables locally, this assignment mutates the global `archive_path` variable set at the script root:

```sh
  archive_path="$tmp_dir/$asset"
  checksum_path="$tmp_dir/$checksum_asset"

  step "Downloading Codex CLI"
  if [ "$install_layout" = "package" ]; then
    checksum_digest="$(release_asset_digest "$checksum_asset")"
    download_file_with_fallback "$checksum_url" "$checksum_fallback_url" "$checksum_path" "$checksum_digest" "$checksum_asset" "$asset"
    expected_digest="$(package_archive_digest "$asset" "$checksum_path")"
  else
    expected_digest="$(release_asset_digest "$asset")"
  fi
  download_file_with_fallback "$download_url" "$download_fallback_url" "$archive_path" "$expected_digest" "$asset"
```

When `download_file_with_fallback` is called for the checksum manifest, it calls `verify_archive_digest "$output" "$expected_digest"` with `$output` = `$checksum_path`.
`verify_archive_digest` executes `archive_path="$1"`, overwriting the global `archive_path` variable to `$checksum_path` (`$tmp_dir/codex-package_SHA256SUMS`).

This causes severe bugs:
1. When `download_file_with_fallback` subsequently downloads the actual package archive (`codex-package-*.tar.gz`), it writes directly to `$archive_path`—which is `$checksum_path`! The package archive completely overwrites and destroys the checksum manifest file on disk.
2. The package archive is never saved under its real name (`codex-package-$vendor_target.tar.gz`).
3. If an archive download fails or encounters an error without writing (or if fallback occurs), `verify_archive_digest` verifies `$checksum_path` (which still contains the checksum manifest text), resulting in bogus checksum mismatch errors:
   `Downloaded Codex archive checksum did not match expected digest.`
   (as previously reported in #49337).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run a minimal script tracing `archive_path` before and after downloading the checksum manifest:

```sh
sh -c '
tmp_dir="/tmp/test_sh_bug"
asset="codex-package-darwin.tar.gz"
checksum_asset="codex-package_SHA256SUMS"

verify_archive_digest() {
  archive_path="$1"
}

archive_path="$tmp_dir/$asset"
checksum_path="$tmp_dir/$checksum_asset"

echo "BEFORE checksum download: archive_path=$archive_path"
verify_archive_digest "$checksum_path"
echo "AFTER  checksum download: archive_path=$archive_path"
'
```

Output:
```
BEFORE checksum download: archive_path=/tmp/test_sh_bug/codex-package-darwin.tar.gz
AFTER  checksum download: archive_path=/tmp/test_sh_bug/codex-package_SHA256SUMS
```

The destination of the package archive is permanently clobbered into the checksum manifest path.

### What is the expected behavior?

`verify_archive_digest` should use a local parameter name (`archive_file="$1"`) so it does not overwrite the global `archive_path` variable.
The checksum manifest and the package archive should be downloaded into two distinct files, and the checksum manifest must remain intact.

### Additional information

Related issue: #49337

We have prepared a tested fix on a fork branch and opened a pull request on the fork (since openai/codex restricts external pull requests):
- **Pull Request on fork:** https://github.com/Saauf/codex/pull/1
- **Commit:** [706b01d](https://github.com/Saauf/codex/commit/706b01d44a0173e4d2f091fe5e3c26681b530ede)
- **Branch:** `fix/install-sh-archive-path-clobbering`

The fix:
1. Renames `archive_path` to `archive_file` in `verify_archive_digest()`.
2. Renames `asset` to `target_asset` in `package_archive_digest()` to avoid variable collision.
3. Adds an automated test in `scripts/install/test_install_sh.py` (`test_package_archive_download_does_not_overwrite_checksum_manifest`) verifying both files are downloaded to distinct destinations.

Maintainers can cherry-pick this fix with:
```bash
git fetch https://github.com/Saauf/codex.git fix/install-sh-archive-path-clobbering
git cherry-pick 706b01d44a0173e4d2f091fe5e3c26681b530ede
```

items.body:
Reproduced on 11 October 2026. Local repair has not been established.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app: 26.1007.21434, build 13901; configured update check reports up_to_date.
- Bundled Windows and Linux Codex CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- WSL 2, Ubuntu, Bash; kernel 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2.
- Windows Codex home is shared with WSL through CODEX_HOME=/mnt/c/Users/<user>/.codex, as documented.
- SQLite files are stored under the Ubuntu home directory.
- Official workspace bundle: 26.1009.11318, targetPlatform win32.
- Official cua_node manifest: Windows x64, node_repl.exe; runtime archive version 0.0.29/20261005054403-144090e2ddcb.

## Reproduction A: normal JavaScript tool fails before executing code

1. Configure the Windows desktop app agent to use WSL; reopen the app manually.
2. Open a chat whose working directory is a Linux path, such as /mnt/e/project.
3. Call the ordinary node_repl/js tool with console.log('JS_BRIDGE_OK').
4. The call fails before executing JavaScript. The following error reproduces the wording, with the real project path anonymized as /mnt/e/project:

    Mcp error: -32602: js: codex/sandbox-state-meta:
    sandboxCwd is not a local file URI: file:///mnt/e/project

The MCP definition invokes the officially installed Windows node_repl.exe through its mounted /mnt/c path. The configured Node, native pipe and CLI environment paths are Windows paths. No replacement runtime has been supplied.

Expected: a supported cross-system bridge, or a clear unsupported-environment message and documented recovery that preserves chats and project paths.

The executable help exposes only --disable-sandbox in addition to help. This flag was NOT used; sandbox isolation must be retained.

## Reproduction B: reserved workspace marketplace restoration fails

Desktop logs repeatedly contain:

    plugin_marketplace_add_failed:
    marketplace `openai-primary-runtime` is reserved and cannot be added from this source
    primary_runtime_restore_failed:
    Failed to sync primary runtime bundled plugin marketplace

The shared configuration identifies this as a local marketplace rooted at the installed Windows primary-runtime plugin directory. Windows CLI lists it; Linux CLI does not. A temporary read-only Linux source override previously did not make the reserved marketplace appear.

This does not prove the workspace bundle is absent: the ordinary desktop load_workspace_dependencies tool successfully reports its paths. The installed Windows Node and Python executables also run from Bash with approved interoperability. Python finds docx, openpyxl, pptx, pypdf and PIL. Those approved checks do NOT establish normal node_repl sandbox compatibility.

The marketplace and MCP sections already existed in nine retained configuration backups. Their original creation date/author cannot be determined. The native pipe value rotated when the app reopened; this alone does not establish provenance of the entire MCP definition.

## Symptom C: models appear slowly when opening a chat

The user reports a new delay in model selection when entering chats. Desktop RPC logs after reopening show:

| Request | Observed duration |
| --- | ---: |
| model/list | 8–48 ms, seven recorded requests |
| plugin/installed | up to 20,012 ms |
| config/read | up to 13,977 ms |
| mcpServerStatus/list | up to 20,993 ms |
| thread/read | up to 39,226 ms |
| thread/resume | up to 48,960 ms |

Read-only CLI comparison:

- Linux plugin list, bundled local marketplace: 1.17 seconds.
- Linux installed plugin list with approved host network: 0.93 seconds, successful.
- Direct shared configuration read: 6.8 ms.

The app plugin/installed RPC and CLI plugin list command are related operations, not a controlled comparison of identical requests. These observations justify investigating the desktop route without identifying the responsible component. A causal link among restoration retries, these RPC waits and visible model-picker latency has NOT been proven. The desktop log records hostId=local state=connected at 18:39:25.522 UTC and nextState=connected at 18:39:25.524 UTC, alongside a connection-failed error field containing MCP resource warnings. A continuing disconnection was not established; these fields do not rule out earlier transient failures.

Desktop logs also contain repeated ResizeObserver loop errors. Their causal relationship to the other symptoms is unknown.

## Preservation and limits

- Normal Bash shell execution and ordinary history reads for two affected projects pass after the manual reopen.
- Their actual project folders are accessible.
- Normal JavaScript bridge remains broken.
- All project workflows and views have NOT been tested in every chat.
- No resets, dependency reinstalls, marketplace deletion, binary edits, environment switch or further app/WSL restart were applied during this joint diagnosis.
- No account tokens, credentials, user transcript content or full raw logs are included here.

## Official guidance consulted

- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-app#windows-subsystem-for-linux-wsl
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-app#share-config-auth-and-sessions-with-wsl
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp#stdio-servers
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference#codex-plugin-marketplace
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic#configuration-precedence
- https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting#feedback-and-logs

## Requested maintainer guidance

Please identify the supported WSL-compatible node_repl integration and reserved-marketplace restoration path for this app build. Please also advise how to diagnose the desktop RPC delays without resetting configuration, deleting chat history or switching existing projects to a different host.

## Subsequent isolated cache-location diagnostic

The official issue-reporting route identifies related public reports #51905 (reserved source and slow plugin enumeration) and #52468 (same node_repl URI rejection). These are user reports, not a verified maintainer remedy.

Four read-only Linux CLI marketplace/list tests were run, without persisting any setting:

| Process-local settings | Primary runtime listed |
| --- | --- |
| Original configuration/environment | No |
| XDG_CACHE_HOME set to the mounted existing Windows cache only | No |
| Temporary -c source override to the mounted primary-runtime plugin root only | No |
| Both process-local cache location and source override | Yes |

This establishes a CLI catalog-discovery difference when both locations agree. It does NOT establish a fix for desktop reconciliation, model-picker latency, Windows/Linux configuration compatibility or node_repl. No XDG setting was added to shell profiles, global Windows variables or the desktop launch environment. Redirecting all Linux caches would affect other apps and conflict with the user's storage preferences.

Related reports:
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51905
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52468

Please identify a supported app-scoped configuration or product fix rather than requiring global cache redirection.

## Earliest retained evidence, not proven onset

A scan of 110 retained desktop log files found:

| Event | Earliest retained evidence (UTC) |
| --- | --- |
| Reserved primary-runtime source rejection / restoration failure | 2026-09-27 00:00:11.836 |
| model/list over 1 second | 2026-09-28 15:33:35.160; 1,840 ms |
| thread/resume over 10 seconds | 2026-09-28 23:08:58.663; 10,757 ms |
| plugin/installed over 10 seconds | 2026-10-05 21:40:12.488; 20,526 ms |
| node_repl URI rejection in this chat's retained tool output | 2026-10-11 09:42:27.408 |

The catalog failure is already present in the oldest available desktop logs. These dates are not a verified regression onset or evidence that all symptoms share a cause.

This is an existing installation after local recovery, not a clean-install reproduction. Earlier recovery included Linux shell-helper path recovery and stored project-path normalization. The ordinary Bash workflow now works; the minimal node_repl call fails independently before JavaScript executes. No raw configuration or conversation history is attached.

items.title: [Desktop] Restore Codex mode when returning to a local project conversation (avoid accidental Work execution)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Summary

The unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop app appears to keep the **ChatGPT vs. Codex execution mode** selected globally instead of restoring the mode associated with the conversation or local project being reopened.

When I temporarily leave an active local Codex task to consult ChatGPT, then return to the Codex conversation, the app can still be in **ChatGPT** mode. Continuing work without manually noticing and switching modes can start a **ChatGPT Work** task instead of continuing in **local Codex**.

This is not merely a tab-selection inconvenience: it can silently change the intended execution environment for a local development project.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In the desktop app, select **Codex**, open a **local repository/project**, and start a coding task.
2. While Codex is running, switch to the **ChatGPT** tab to research or discuss the next steps.
3. When the Codex task completes, navigate back to its conversation/project.
4. Notice that the top-level execution mode **remains ChatGPT** rather than automatically returning to Codex.
5. Attempt to continue the original coding task. Without manually switching the mode back, the follow-up can be sent through **Work** rather than Codex.

## Actual behavior

The selected execution mode is not reliably restored to match the local Codex conversation/project the user returns to. The app makes it possible to inadvertently launch the follow-up task in Work.

## Expected behavior

- Reopening a **local Codex** conversation/project should automatically restore **Codex mode** (ideally persisted per conversation, or at least per project).
- An explicit user decision to use another environment should still be possible.
- As a safety fallback, warn or require confirmation before executing an apparent Codex-local follow-up using **Work**.

## Why this matters

Local Codex tasks are commonly tied to a specific execution context:

- Working directory, local files, repository and Git worktree state.
- Locally installed CLI tools, dependencies and MCP servers.
- Project instructions (e.g., `AGENTS.md`) and global/user configuration.
- Permissions, environment variables, and task/session state.

**Work may not have the same environment, tools, configurations, permissions, or local project state.** A task launched in the wrong execution environment may produce inconsistent results or fail unexpectedly. It may also consume **unexpected Work/Codex usage or tokens** before the user recognizes the mismatch.

The important distinction is that the user **did not intend to switch the execution environment of the original project**; they only switched to a different conversation temporarily.

## Suggested solution

Associate the execution mode with its conversation or local project and restore that mode when navigating back. At a minimum, make the destination environment unmistakable and show a confirmation before launching Work for an existing local Codex project.

> Switching conversations should not silently change the execution environment of an existing project.

## Related issues

- #40963 — Project-scoped Work/Codex environments instead of app-global or session-derived mode.
- #41594 — Desktop labels conflate Chat, Work, and Codex tasks.

## Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex unified desktop application.
- Specific application version/build not captured.

The browser-control tools in Codex fail during initialization, preventing the agent from inspecting browser tabs or testing my local web application.
The latest error is:
MXC launcher: cannot locate required Windows platform directory: HRESULT 0x80070003
The process exits with code 1 when the agent invokes cua.getState(). Other attempts returned:
trusted Node process exited unexpectedly; kernel reset, rerun your request
The same initialization error occurred when testing Google Chrome and the Codex integrated browser separately. No browser state or tab handle was returned.
The desktop connection itself is available. The Chrome extension is installed and enabled, and the native-host registry entry and manifest were verified. The exact cause of the runtime failure is still unknown.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected Windows installation:
1. Open the Codex desktop app and connect the computer to the task.
2. Open Google Chrome with the ChatGPT browser extension enabled.
3. Ask the agent to inspect the available browser tabs using its supported browser tools.
4. The agent invokes cua.getState(), but initialization fails with HRESULT 0x80070003 before returning browser state.
The failure also occurred when requesting an integrated-browser tab using cua.createBrowserTab("iab", "http://127.0.0.1:8088/", { visible: true }).
This is reproducible on my machine. I have not confirmed reproduction on another computer or a clean Windows installation. No application login is reached.

### What is the expected behavior?

The browser-control runtime should initialize and return the available browser state. The agent should then be able to access an authorized Chrome tab or open a tab in the integrated browser.
If a required Windows component or directory is missing, the error should identify it and provide an actionable recovery procedure.

### Additional information

Installed versions reported by local diagnostics:
- Codex MSIX package: 26.1007.2314.0
- Bundled Codex CLI: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- Browser / Computer Use / CUA components: 26.1007.21434
Troubleshooting already performed:
- Restarted Chrome.
- Restarted Codex.
- Restarted the entire PC.
- Reinstalled Codex dependencies.
- Checked for Codex updates; none were available.
- Tested Chrome and the integrated browser separately.
A diagnostic initially reported a missing native-host registration, but this was a false negative: it looked for “(Default)” while Spanish Windows returned “(Predeterminado)”. The registry entry and manifest were subsequently verified. The isolated execution environment also uses a different LOCALAPPDATA path.
An older task referenced component version 26.1002.52244, while installed manifests referenced 26.1007.21434. A newer task exposes CUA but fails during initialization. It is not established whether these observations share a root cause.
Earlier browser testing worked through a separate direct-debugging script. That was a different access method, so it does not establish that the currently failing integrated runtime previously worked.
I would appreciate a supported recovery procedure that preserves projects, browser profiles and application settings.

items.title: Cloud sandbox restrictions block dependency installation and Chromium startup

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Impact

This is a showstopper for our workflow. We cannot install required dependencies or use browser automation, preventing us from completing our work in this cloud environment.

The intended task was to install yt-dlp and faster-whisper in an isolated Python virtual environment, download audio from two YouTube videos while respecting access restrictions, convert it with ffmpeg, and transcribe it. The browser transcript fallback also failed before page navigation.

## Environment and observed failures

This is a managed Linux cloud environment with a workspace-write command sandbox, not a confirmed reproduction on a particular standalone Codex CLI release. The CLI version was not collected.

At the latest status check, the environment service reported running, connected, observations_current=true, network_policy.mode=unrestricted, and network_policy.state=enforced.

Package installation failed with:

```text
ProxyError: Cannot connect to proxy
Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted
```

A subsequent ordinary Python urllib request to https://pypi.org/simple/yt-dlp/ failed with:

```text
URLError: <urlopen error [Errno 1] Operation not permitted>
```

A scoped network-enabled installation retry was requested but canceled by the user. It therefore does not establish whether a granted network permission would resolve package installation.

## Chromium startup failure

Playwright launched /usr/bin/chromium headlessly. Chromium terminated before opening a page. The startup log reported:

```text
third_party/crashpad/crashpad/util/linux/socket.cc:45
setsockopt: Operation not permitted (1)
```

The process then exited with SIGTRAP.

Separate minimal tests in the ordinary command sandbox confirmed that both Internet socket creation and setsockopt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_PASSCRED) on a local Unix socket pair fail with [Errno 1] Operation not permitted.

Run each example separately:

```python
import socket
socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
```

```python
import socket
a, b = socket.socketpair()
a.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_PASSCRED, 1)
```

## Related report

These browser symptoms closely match https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47452, which reports a Linux sandbox filter blocking Chromium's local startup communication. This suggests a related compatibility issue, although we have not confirmed the underlying implementation cause in our managed environment. The network restriction and browser startup failure may require separate fixes.

## Requested resolution

Please investigate the effective command permissions and Chromium startup failure, and provide a supported way to run dependency installation and browser automation in this environment. It would also help if the environment status clearly distinguished its network policy from the permissions actually applied to commands.

We are comfortable with a complete reset and recreation of the virtual machine for this cloud instance if that would help resolve the issue. We suspect an initialization or configuration problem during the initial setup, but this remains unconfirmed. A fresh environment would help determine whether the failures are specific to this instance or reflect a broader sandbox compatibility issue.

No audio was downloaded or transcribed. No production applications or global Python packages were modified. This report describes a blocker for this workflow and instance; it does not establish that all cloud environments are affected.

items.title: [Windows App] GPT-5.5 migration notice repeats after selecting GPT-6.1 Sol; High intermittently resets to Medium

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
## Summary

Codex desktop repeatedly displays the GPT-5.5 retirement/migration notice even after I have manually selected GPT-6.1 Sol. My selected reasoning effort also intermittently changes from High to Medium.

A local inspection found both repeated persisted migration notices for the same conversation and High-to-Medium changes in runtime turn metadata. The stale global default may be relevant, but the logs inspected do not identify the component that changes the selection.

## Environment

- Windows, native Codex desktop (MSIX).
- Installed package version: `26.1007.2314.0`.
- Bundled runtime version recorded in local thread state: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- Selected model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Intended reasoning effort: `high`.
- Observed on 12 October 2026, timezone UTC+08:00.

## What I see

The app repeatedly shows the Chinese notice:

> GPT-5.5即将停用，此对话已改用GPT-6.1SOL

I had already selected GPT-6.1 Sol manually. I also select High, but later find the selector at Medium. This continues across multiple conversations.

## Local evidence

### Persisted migration state

The local `.codex-global-state.json` contains:

```json
{
  "model-upgrade-decisions": {
    "gpt-5.5": "switched"
  }
}
```

Despite that decision, `model-upgrade-transcript-notices` contains multiple entries for the same conversation at different turn IDs. Each entry has:

```json
{
  "replacementModelName": "GPT-6.1 Sol",
  "retiringModelName": "GPT-5.5",
  "wasRetired": false
}
```

In the inspected snapshot, one conversation had six entries and two others had two entries each. Conversation and turn identifiers are omitted here.

### Runtime turn metadata

The local `logs_2.sqlite` records the following model and `codex.turn.reasoning_effort` values. A and B stand for distinct conversations; each pair is within the same conversation.

| Time on 2026-10-12 (UTC+08:00) | Conversation | Model | Turn reasoning effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01:53:05 | A | gpt-6.1-sol | high |
| 02:16:32 | A | gpt-6.1-sol | medium |
| 02:23:15 | B | gpt-6.1-sol | high |
| 02:24:24 | B | gpt-6.1-sol | medium |

These are runtime turn metadata, rather than an inference from the picker alone. They do not by themselves establish which component changed the effort, nor are they a raw upstream request capture.

### Global configuration before the workaround

The user-level `config.toml` still contained:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.5"
```

There was no top-level `model_reasoning_effort`, and no active top-level profile. The inspected current project directory had no `.codex/config.toml`.

The model cache advertised a GPT-5.5 upgrade to GPT-6.1 Sol with retirement at `2026-10-14T19:00:00Z`. GPT-6.1 Sol's cached supported efforts include High, so High is an available selection.

## Observed reproduction pattern

1. Have an existing desktop installation with a user-level GPT-5.5 default.
2. Manually select GPT-6.1 Sol / High in the composer.
3. Continue using existing conversations.
4. Observe another GPT-5.5-to-Sol migration notice and, intermittently, a later turn at Medium.

This is the pattern observed in a live installation, not a confirmed clean-profile reproduction. Exact triggering conditions remain unknown.

## Expected behavior

- Once a conversation is already using GPT-6.1 Sol, the app should not repeatedly announce that it has just migrated that conversation from GPT-5.5.
- An explicit High selection should remain effective until I change it.
- Migration/default reconciliation should not silently replace an explicitly selected supported reasoning effort.

## Workaround attempted

After capturing the evidence, I backed up the user-level config and changed only:

```toml
model = "gpt-6.1-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"
```

The resulting TOML was parsed and verified. No app restart, conversation database edits, or persisted UI-state edits were performed. Whether this prevents recurrence is not yet verified.

Possibly related: #36163, #34535, #14008. This report adds the repeated retirement notices together with runtime High-to-Medium transitions.

No credentials, full configuration files, raw conversation content, or private filesystem paths are included.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: mcp

labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Environment

- Windows desktop Codex, using the Code Mode functions.exec surface. Model identity is not independently recorded in this report.
- Running desktop Codex runtime, verified from its executable: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- An older CLI bundled separately reports 0.142.4; this report uses the running desktop runtime for protocol and transport checks.
- Desktop application version and subscription tier are not collected.
- Connected remote OAuth MCP server. Server product, host names, account/workspace/resource identifiers, chat IDs and local paths are omitted.

## Problem and observed evidence

A fresh native desktop chat can discover five related MCP tools and make harmless authenticated reads. However, its supported model-visible ALL_TOOLS entries contain only name and description, including generated TypeScript declarations. No enabled assistant tool exports the current chat's complete raw inputSchema, standard annotations or schema-reference _meta.

This prevents strict client capability verification for two read tools and three command tools with different consequential classifications. Tool names and rendered TypeScript do not establish nested schema constraints, annotations or the client-registered schema reference. A server-reported capability manifest is separate evidence.

The installed desktop binary's app-server generate-json-schema --experimental output already defines:

- mcpServerStatus/list parameters including threadId, serverName and detail.
- Tool properties including inputSchema, annotations and _meta.

Thus the native core protocol already represents the required metadata. Generated protocol schemas do not prove that the current desktop catalog was exported.

The documented codex app-server proxy command, using the desktop runtime binary, fails to connect to the default control socket with Windows error 10061 (connection actively refused). A read-only process check finds three app-server processes explicitly using stdio and one without a listener argument; none advertises a Unix or TCP listener in its command arguments. The documented default transport is stdio. This does not rule out every custom route, nor does it prove an MCP server or host-cache defect.

An older implementation chat exposes four of the five tools; the earlier fresh verifier exposes all five. These are separate snapshots. The report's main request concerns metadata access, not a proven tool-discovery regression.

## Reproduction in the observed setup

1. Use a native desktop chat with an enabled, authenticated MCP server providing tools with schemas, standard annotations and a namespaced _meta schema reference.
2. Inspect matching entries and Object.keys(entry) in the supported ALL_TOOLS inventory. Observe names/descriptions without raw metadata.
3. Verify the connected service through a harmless read. Keep this evidence separate from client metadata evidence.
4. Generate JSON protocol schemas from the running desktop runtime. Observe that the native API already defines the missing metadata fields.
5. Attempt the documented proxy connection to the existing app server. In this Windows setup, the default control socket refuses the connection before a chat-scoped metadata request can be made.

This is an observed reproduction, not a deterministic clean-install fixture. No app restart, daemon bootstrap, listener/config change, direct MCP HTTP request, credential copying, cache scraping or command-tool execution was used.

## Requested change

Please route this to the Codex desktop/Code Mode interface owner and provide a supported read-only assistant capability to export metadata from the current chat's existing MCP connection and tool catalog, reusing mcpServerStatus/list rather than creating an independent session.

For selected tools, return complete registered inputSchema, standard annotations and allowlisted schema-reference metadata, plus observation/catalog provenance. Explicitly distinguish undiscovered tools and unavailable fields. A documented native export path callable from this Windows desktop environment would also resolve the evidence gap.

Exclude tool-call arguments/results, credentials, account/customer/resource values and browser state. Keep existing host approval, authorization, expiry and execution controls intact.

## Acceptance and retest

1. The assistant retrieves one supported snapshot of the current native chat's five tools, with clear provenance.
2. All five complete input schemas are inspectable, or independently verifiable hashes have a documented algorithm/canonicalization and matching accessible schema.
3. Standard annotations and exact namespaced schema references are preserved and can be compared with the connected product contract.
4. A bounded read-only comparison of all five returns no missing or mismatched fields; no prepare, confirmation or execution write is necessary.

Current status: declaration discovery and harmless reads passed in the fresh verifier; strict client metadata verification remains blocked. No fix or post-fix pass is claimed.

Reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server
Core implementation: https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs/app-server

No raw logs, screenshots, private transcripts, credentials, local paths or account/resource identifiers are attached.

## Passing synthetic confirmation/apply fixture proof

Added 11 October 2026. Evidence class: technical, local in-memory integration testing.

An isolated fixture uses a Draft campaign, a Draft social asset and a manual, unmeasured outcome with one social placement. It prepares an owner-report command with this synthetic-only note:

> [SYNTHETIC TEST] Confirmation receipt only. Nothing was posted, sent or delivered.

No public URL, destination or schedule is supplied. The command requires confirmation while the campaign and asset remain Draft. Tests exercise the registered MCP transport, the real OAuth adapter seam and in-memory Convex transactions. Outbound fetch is configured to throw; approval responses are synthetic and programmatic.

| Scenario | Result and verified behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Local tool metadata | Passed: all five registered server tools expose complete input schemas, standard annotations and exact versioned schema references; confirmation fields and strict object constraints match the application contract. |
| Legacy exact-review confirmation | Passed: confirmation itself performs no campaign mutation, expiry is bounded and does not renew on repeat, a wrong confirmation ID is rejected, apply executes once, and replay returns the same receipt/version. |
| Initialized native acceptance | Passed on protocol 2025-06-18: the synthetic approval prompt occurs before mutation, acceptance permits one exact apply, and replay recovers the receipt. |
| Initialized native decline | Passed on protocol 2025-06-18: declining performs no execution or campaign mutation. |

Vitest structured result: **4 passed, 0 failed, success=true**. Fixture lint and application typecheck also passed. The synthetic campaign and asset remain Draft; unrelated sentinel campaign state and all asset rows are compared before/after. No real campaigns were touched and no hosted prepare, confirmation or apply call was performed.

The tested fixture source has SHA-256 `95ef3352a701cf5141ad7c768d25a2e65b8e92f2511ff4f1eeb76af5fa8de871`. Source and structured results are retained locally; the digest identifies that artifact and is not a public reproduction download.

This fixture proves the application confirmation/apply behavior in isolation. It does not prove a live desktop approval, hosted execution or current-chat metadata export, and it does not reproduce the desktop transport failure. The local server schema snapshot is an implementation reference, not a substitute for the missing client-registered metadata.

### Exact unblock step

Expose a supported read-only assistant bridge to the existing native chat's `mcpServerStatus/list`, scoped to that chat and its already connected MCP server. Return the five tools' complete `inputSchema`, standard `annotations`, allowlisted schema-reference `_meta`, and observation/catalog provenance. A documented native export path callable in this Windows desktop setup is also sufficient.

Once that export is available, compare all five tools once against the application contract. Only after the comparison passes can the live confirmation/apply test proceed on a newly created, explicitly synthetic Draft fixture, with the exact native human confirmation and before/after readback. Keep every pre-existing campaign unchanged; do not publish, activate, generate paid content or send anything.

items.title: [macOS Desktop] Persistent access-denied background hydration retries alongside high renderer CPU; restart does not resolve

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### Environment

Observed October 11, 2026 on macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple Silicon.
- Codex Framework: `155.0.8059.40`
- Desktop build: `20156`
- Build commit: `a993bdbe5bb9503cb84de1e67d5635cf186a959f`

The version above was obtained from a process sample and desktop logs, rather than the About dialog.

### Issue

While investigating a lightly used Mac running warm, Codex's renderer was observed using 59–100% CPU (one logical core). Desktop logs show persistent background `thread/read` requests failing with `-32003: thread access denied`, repeatedly targeting the same chats.

A full app restart reduced immediate renderer CPU but did not stop the denied-read loop.

### Observed sequence

This is an existing-profile observation, not a clean-install reproducer:

1. With Desktop open under light user interaction, inspect process CPU and app logs.
2. Observe repeated failures with:
   ```text
   method=thread/read
   source=thread_hydration
   priority=background
   error.code=-32003
   error.message="thread access denied"
   failureReason=null
   ```
3. Fully quit and restart the desktop app.
4. Observe the same denied background reads return immediately.
5. Use the supported `set_thread_read_state(hostId="durable", read=true)` tool for one affected chat. Its associated `thread/read` succeeds (`errorCode=null`), but background hydration reads for the same ID continue failing. Marking the chat read does not stop those retries.

### Measurements

- **2,007 failed background hydration requests across 96 chat IDs** in a 14-minute window (10:55–11:09 AM Pacific).
- **35,374 denied hydration error rows** across the inspected previous-run logs, spanning approximately 18 hours. This is a log-row count; unique request IDs across the entire run were not independently recounted.
- Repeated failures for one example target occurred about **every five seconds**.
- **496 denied hydration errors within the first 25 seconds** of the restarted run.
- Renderer CPU samples before restart: **59% and 100.2%**. A later sample fell to **11%**.
- Renderer CPU shortly after restart: **6.7%**, while denied reads continued.
- macOS reported no recorded thermal or performance warning.

These observations establish unnecessary repeated requests and CPU spikes in the same app run. They do **not** prove the retry loop causes every spike, sustained CPU saturation, or thermal throttling. Another cloud chat was actively running during diagnosis.

### Read-only inspection lead — not a confirmed root cause

Inspection of shipped JavaScript found:
- `hydratePinnedThreads` explicitly supplies `threadAccess: "shared"` for the durable host.
- The general hydration path obtains access mode from an already-loaded conversation. An unloaded conversation can therefore reach a read without that explicit mode.
- `readThread` retains terminal cached errors for normalized `thread_not_found`, but not access denial.
- The memoized hydration read removes its entry in `finally`, including rejected reads.

An access-mode/transport mismatch and insufficient suppression or backoff are plausible leads. Actual wire payloads and backend authorization decisions were not captured; the exact caller initiating the five-second refresh has not been identified.

### Expected behavior

- Preserve the correct authorized access mode for shared cloud chats during background loading.
- Treat authorization denial as a bounded unavailable state rather than retrying indefinitely without an access/identity change or explicit user retry.
- Coordinate retries across renderers and provide a supported recovery that preserves chats and active work.
- Preserve server authorization boundaries.

### Related reports

- #51675: macOS cloud sidebar disappearance, denied hydration, and successful same-target direct reads.
- #51572: repeated access-denied Desktop hydration on Windows.
- #52129: Windows direct-read/UI-hydration contrast.

Please consolidate if appropriate. This report adds observations from build 20156, measured CPU spikes, long-running retry volume, and immediate recurrence after restart.

### Uploaded feedback session

`019c0d37-d2b6-74c0-918f-0e64af9b6e14` (ID supplied by the app's prefilled GitHub feedback link).

### Privacy and interventions

No raw logs, credentials, account identifiers, private chat IDs/titles, conversation contents, or local paths are attached. No application binaries, credential stores, server ACLs, or chat databases were modified. One affected chat was marked read as the diagnostic test described above.

---

**Attribution:** Investigated, drafted, and submitted by Codex, the AI assistant running in the ChatGPT desktop app, on behalf of @arrhen and with their authorization. Measurements came from local process samples and application logs; interpretations and limitations are identified above.

items.title: Desktop sidebar keeps threads archived/deleted outside the UI (catalog never fully reconciles)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
The desktop sidebar reads `~/.codex/sqlite/codex-dev.db` → `local_thread_catalog`. `isFullReconciliationDue()` is only true when `last_full_reconciled_at IS NULL`, so after the initial build the catalog is only incrementally updated.

**Result:** threads archived via `codex archive` or removed via `codex delete` stay listed in the sidebar indefinitely. In my case: 1113 stale entries (553 deleted + 560 archived) vs 176 real ones; `state_5.sqlite` was correct (`archived = 1`, rollouts moved to `archived_sessions/`).

**Workaround:** with the app closed, `UPDATE local_thread_catalog_sync_state SET last_full_reconciled_at = NULL WHERE host_id = 'local'` and restart → full reconciliation, sidebar correct (1289 → 176).

**Suggestion:** periodic full reconciliation, or have the app catalog react to archive/delete performed through the CLI / app-server.

**Related:** the Claude session import (`external-agent-import-sync-*`) has no path/pattern exclusion, so tool-generated transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/` (e.g. claude-mem observer sessions, `claude -p` probes) get imported as chats. An exclusion list (paths or globs) would avoid that.

App version 26.1007.21159, macOS (Apple Silicon).

items.title: [Windows][Codex App/CLI] Sandboxed native directory traversal fails with ACCESS DENIED (WinError 5), while Full Access works

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? Version 26.1007.21434 ### What subscription do you have? Not provided ### What platform is your computer? Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64 ### What issue are you seeing?

Summary

Codex Desktop on Windows fails to execute native filesystem directory changes inside its normal Workspace Write sandbox, even when the target directory is readable and belongs to an authorized workspace.

The same operations succeed immediately when switching Codex to Full Access.

This is not specific to Flutter. The problem affects CMD, Git, and the Windows native current-directory API. Flutter and Dart failures are downstream consequences.

Actual behavior

Inside Codex with Workspace Write permissions:

Test 1 — Native CMD directory access

cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d C:\Tools\flutter && cd"

Result:

Access is denied.
Exit code: 1

Test 2 — Native CMD access to an existing project workspace

cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\Projects\<workspace> && cd"

Result:

Access is denied.
Exit code: 1

Test 3 — Git repository access

git -C C:\Tools\flutter rev-parse HEAD

Result:

fatal: cannot change to 'C:\Tools\flutter': Permission denied
Exit code: 1

Test 4 — Windows native current-directory API

[System.IO.Directory]::SetCurrentDirectory('C:\Tools\flutter')

Result:

MethodInvocationException:
Exception calling "SetCurrentDirectory" with "1" argument(s):
"Access to the path 'C:\Tools\flutter' is denied."

PowerShell can access the same directory

Interestingly, these operations succeed inside the same sandbox:

Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'C:\Tools\flutter' -Name

Set-Location -LiteralPath 'C:\Tools\flutter'

Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\Tools\flutter\.git\HEAD' -TotalCount 1

Git itself launches correctly:

git version 2.56.0.windows.2

This suggests that ordinary filesystem reading works, while native directory-handle operations fail.

Impact on Flutter development

Running flutter --version inside Codex produces:

fatal: cannot change to 'C:\Tools\flutter': Permission denied

Invoke-Expression:
C:\Tools\flutter\bin\internal\update_engine_version.ps1:62

You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression.

Error: Unable to determine engine version...

Some Flutter and Dart commands also hang until manually terminated.

However, Flutter, Dart, Git, and native CMD directory changes work correctly outside Codex and in Full Access mode.

Process Monitor evidence

Microsoft Sysinternals Process Monitor captured the exact filesystem failures.

First denial — Codex's bundled PowerShell runtime

Process: cmd.exe
Operation: CreateFile

Path:
C:\Users\<USER>\.cache\codex-runtimes\
codex-primary-runtime\dependencies\native\powershell

Result: ACCESS DENIED

Desired Access: Execute/Traverse, Synchronize
Disposition: Open
Options: Directory, Synchronous IO Non-Alert

Second denial — Flutter SDK

Process: cmd.exe
PID: 23544
Operation: CreateFile
Path: C:\Tools\flutter

Result: ACCESS DENIED

Desired Access: Execute/Traverse, Synchronize
Disposition: Open
Options: Directory, Synchronous IO Non-Alert

The captured process sequence:

codex.exe
    |
    v
pwsh.exe
    |
    v
cmd.exe
    |
    v
CreateFile(C:\Tools\flutter)
    |
    v
ACCESS DENIED (WinError 5)

The first access denial involves Codex's own runtime directory, before the Flutter SDK denial.

Therefore, this is not merely a missing Flutter SDK permission.

ProcMon establishes the denied access request but does not identify the precise Windows security rule responsible.

Full Access comparison

Running the identical tests in Codex Full Access mode:

Command | Workspace Write | Full Access -- | -- | -- CMD change to project directory | FAIL | PASS CMD change to Flutter SDK | FAIL | PASS Git read Flutter revision | FAIL | PASS flutter --version | FAIL | PASS dart --version | FAIL | PASS flutter analyze execution | FAIL / timeout | Completes

In Full Access, Flutter 3.47.7 and Dart 3.13.5 initialize normally. Static analysis also completes; separate missing-dependency diagnostics are unrelated to this sandbox issue.

The sandbox boundary is the distinguishing factor.

### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Install Codex Desktop on Windows 11. 2. Open an existing local development project. 3. Select **Workspace Write** permissions, not Full Access. 4. Ask Codex to execute: ```powershell cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d C:\Tools\flutter && cd" ``` 5. Observe: ```text Access is denied. Exit code: 1 ``` 6. Test an existing project workspace: ```powershell cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d D:\Projects\ && cd" ``` 7. Observe the same error. 8. Run: ```powershell [System.IO.Directory]::SetCurrentDirectory('C:\Tools\flutter') ``` 9. Observe a Windows access-denied exception. 10. Switch Codex to **Full Access**. 11. Repeat the same CMD and Git tests. They succeed immediately. The problem reproduces after a complete Codex uninstall, removal of previous generated sandbox/runtime components, and a clean reinstall. No source-code modification is required to reproduce the issue. Session ID and token/context-window usage were not captured. The issue is reproducible independently of model context usage. ### Additional reproduction: Standalone Codex CLI I also tested the standalone Codex CLI, launched from normal Windows PowerShell outside Codex Desktop. The CLI reproduces the same native directory-access failure under Workspace Write sandbox permissions. Therefore, the issue is not exclusive to the Codex Desktop application. Both Desktop and CLI exhibit the failure, while commands work outside Codex or with Full Access. This suggests a problem in their shared Windows sandbox implementation or its interaction with the host Windows security environment. The exact underlying security rule responsible for the denial remains unidentified. ### What is the expected behavior? Codex in Workspace Write mode should be able to execute native Windows commands and change the current working directory to an authorized project workspace or a readable external development SDK. Basic commands such as these should work without requiring Full Access: ```powershell cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d C:\Tools\flutter && cd" git -C C:\Tools\flutter rev-parse HEAD flutter --version dart --version flutter pub get flutter analyze ``` The sandbox should continue protecting unauthorized filesystem locations and restricting unsafe operations. Users should not need to disable sandbox isolation just to run standard development tools. A permanent fix should preserve Workspace Write security rather than require `danger-full-access`. ### Additional information ### Environment - Product: Codex Desktop App for Windows - OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64 - Workspace Dependencies version: 26.1009.11318 - Bundled Node.js and Python tools: Enabled - Subscription: ChatGPT Go - Flutter: 3.47.7 stable - Dart: 3.13.5 - Git: 2.56.0.windows.2 - Sandbox permissions: Workspace Write - Sandboxed process integrity: Low Mandatory Level ### Background Codex previously worked correctly with Flutter and other development tools before an SSD replacement and software environment reinstallation. After the replacement, Flutter was installed at `C:\Tools\flutter`. However, the error also occurs inside a development project on D:, so it is not exclusively related to the Flutter SDK location. ### Troubleshooting already attempted I have extensively investigated this issue. **Sandbox configuration:** - Tested `unelevated` Windows sandbox. - Tested `elevated` Windows sandbox. - Tested the MXC sandbox option. - Executed the elevated sandbox provisioning procedure. - Expanded `writable_roots` to include the entire Flutter SDK. - Confirmed the issue persists inside an authorized project workspace. **Windows permissions:** - Verified inherited NTFS directory ACLs. - Temporarily granted Read & Execute to `Everyone`. - Temporarily granted Read & Execute to `CodexSandboxUsers`. - Neither change fixed the problem. - Restored and verified the original NTFS permissions afterward. The original Flutter directory ACLs include: ```text BUILTIN\Administrators: Full Control NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM: Full Control BUILTIN\Users: Read & Execute NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users: Modify ``` **Sandbox diagnostics:** - Confirmed the sandbox runs at Low Mandatory Integrity Level. - Verified PowerShell file listing and reading succeed. - Verified native `SetCurrentDirectory` fails. - Captured Windows `CreateFile` failures with Process Monitor. - Inspected sandbox setup logs. - Verified the persisted sandbox ACL-state JSON is syntactically valid. - Attempted Windows File System failure auditing; no matching Event 4656 was recorded. The temporary audit rules were removed, and the original audit policy was restored. **Fresh installation:** - Completely uninstalled Codex. - Removed old runtime files and generated sandbox components. - Reinstalled Codex. - Repeated the same tests with a fresh installation. - The exact permission failure remained. This suggests the problem is not simply a corrupted project configuration or broken Flutter installation. ### Related GitHub issues - #29688 — Windows PowerShell cwd / PSDrive initialization bug - #52593 — Windows sandbox native path-resolution EPERM - #15038 — Flutter commands fail or hang inside the sandbox These may be related, but the precise root cause of this reproduction has not been established. ### Request to the Codex team Could you investigate why a sandboxed native Windows process is denied `Execute/Traverse, Synchronize` when opening directories that should be accessible, including authorized workspaces and Codex's own bundled runtime directory? Specifically, could this originate from: - Incorrect restricted-token or sandbox SID access checks? - Mandatory integrity policies? - Native subprocess initialization? - Windows filesystem filter enforcement? - A regression in Windows sandbox permission handling? Please provide a supported fix or configuration mechanism that restores these native filesystem operations **without requiring Full Access**. This issue blocks ordinary development workflows across Flutter, Dart, Git, and other native Windows tools.

items.title: Allow restarting managed background servers from the TUI
items.body:
Allow restarting managed background servers from the TUI

## Why

Startup configuration warnings can reflect settings from when the background server started, even after those settings have been fixed. A restart lets users refresh the server without leaving the TUI.

## What changed

- Add a confirmed restart action to `/daemon`, warning that active or queued work in other chats may be interrupted. Reconnect automatically and let an in-progress restart finish if the TUI exits.
- Verify that Codex manages a local server before enabling restart, including servers discovered with auto-start disabled and those started by `codex agents`.
- Show a restart hint on the first startup configuration warning for managed servers, preserving the original diagnostic for copying and dismissal.
- Repaint the full surface of centered dialogs to restore background colors over cached blank cells.

## Testing

Add CLI integration coverage for agents startup and restarting a discovered daemon with auto-start disabled. Extend TUI tests for confirmation, cancellation, unmanaged servers, warning hints and dismissal, and dialog background rendering.

### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Opening the Codex chat in VS Code's right-hand Secondary Side Bar interferes with mouse text selection inside Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) code cells.

When I click and drag to select part of a line, the selection behaves incorrectly. Sometimes only the initial character or a small portion is selected, while matching occurrences elsewhere are highlighted.

The issue disappears immediately when I close the Codex chat panel, without restarting VS Code.

This affects Jupyter notebook cells. Mouse selection in regular Python (`.py`) files works normally.

### Screen recording

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13dfdd0a-8531-488d-a4e5-0af8177384d5

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open VS Code on Windows 11 with the Codex and Jupyter extensions installed and enabled.
2. Open any Jupyter notebook (`.ipynb`) containing Python code cells.
3. Open the Codex chat in the right-hand Secondary Side Bar.
4. Click inside a code cell and attempt to select part of a line by dragging the mouse across the text.
5. Observe that text selection behaves incorrectly, selecting only part of the intended text or highlighting matching occurrences.
6. Close the Codex chat panel and repeat the same mouse selection. It works normally.
7. Reopen Codex in the right sidebar. The issue returns.
8. Move Codex using **Move To → Panel**, placing it in the bottom panel.
9. Repeat the mouse selection with Codex still open. It now works normally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Mouse dragging should select the intended continuous range of text inside Jupyter notebook code cells, regardless of whether the Codex chat is open or where its panel is docked.

Opening Codex in the Secondary Side Bar should not change normal text-selection behavior.

### Additional information

**Environment**
- OS: Windows 11, x64 (Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0)
- IDE: Visual Studio Code
- Codex IDE extension version: 26.1007.21434
- Affected file type: Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`)

**Troubleshooting performed**
- Reloading VS Code with extensions disabled restores normal mouse selection.
- Enabling the Codex extension without opening its chat does not cause the issue.
- Opening Codex in the right-hand Secondary Side Bar reproduces the issue.
- Closing Codex immediately restores normal selection.
- Moving Codex to the bottom panel resolves the issue while keeping Codex open.
- Regular `.py` files are unaffected.

**Workaround**

Keep the Codex chat docked in the bottom panel instead of the Secondary Side Bar.

The behavior is reproducible without restarting VS Code or modifying the notebook.
